## Batch 219 job 1: rational refinement and UV trimming

Compared Wolfgang Boehm, *Inserting new knots into B-spline curves* (1980), https://doi.org/10.1016/0010-4485(80)90154-2 ; Les Piegl and Wayne Tiller, *Software-engineering approach to degree elevation of B-spline curves* (1994), https://doi.org/10.1016/0010-4485(94)90004-3 ; Les Piegl and Arnaud Richard, *Tessellating trimmed NURBS surfaces* (1995), https://doi.org/10.1016/0010-4485(95)90749-6 ; and William L. Luken, *Tessellation of trimmed NURB surfaces* (1996), https://research.ibm.com/publications/tessellation-of-trimmed-nurb-surfaces . Additional mathematical reference: Nicholas Patrikalakis, Takashi Maekawa and Wonjoon Cho, *Shape Interrogation for Computer Aided Design and Manufacturing*, section 1.4.3 (2009), https://web.mit.edu/hyperbook/Patrikalakis-Maekawa-Cho/node18.html . No companion or rival source read.

Combined design: homogeneous Boehm insertion, endpoint clamping, Bezier segment elevation, then inverse insertion to restore the original continuity with multiplicity increased only by the degree increment. Surfaces apply the same operation to control-net lines. Trimming clips polygonal contours and holes against knot-aware UV cells, constrained-triangulates each retained piece, and evaluates the rational surface. Unlike the model-space tolerance theorem in Piegl/Richard, this API uses explicit surface resolution and claims only UV chord tolerance for trim curves. Existing polygon snap rounding bounds UV boolean resolution. Original mathematical fixtures, no demo and no downloaded assets. Local outside CAD repository absent and its GitHub README inaccessible; no external implementation is adopted.

Batch 219 one-sided evaluation: Carl de Boor, *On Calculating with B-Splines* (1972), https://doi.org/10.1016/0021-9045(72)90080-9 , and Les Piegl and Wayne Tiller, *The NURBS Book* (1997), https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-59223-2 , establish knot multiplicity and recurrence limits. Combined with the trimming papers above, cell endpoints must select their own span on both axes. NurbsSurface.derivatives now accepts leftU/leftV (default false); trimmed geometry uses those exact limits for position and normal. The regression has two disconnected planes separated by a fully repeated u or v knot and fails against the previous default-right-only method. No tolerance was loosened.

Combined design: an optional AreaPicking subclass enters the engine's existing serialized pick context using a request-local Symbol carried by its copied RenderView. The package renderer accepts an optional region target, preserving the original 3x3 point path. One cropped region pass renders current visible triangle IDs with the existing alpha/deformation/instance replay, then one aligned buffer copy and map feeds a scanline even-odd lasso filter. ## Culling WebGL2 occlusion (batch 223 job 1)

Clean-room CPU depth testing combines Ned Greene, Michael Kass and Gavin Miller,
*Hierarchical Z-Buffer Visibility*, SIGGRAPH 1993,
https://www.cs.cmu.edu/afs/cs/academic/class/15869-f11/www/readings/greene93_hierarchicalz.pdf
with Jon Hasselgren, Tomas Akenine-Moller and Lennart Ohlsson,
*Conservative Rasterization*, GPU Gems 2, 2005,
https://developer.nvidia.com/gpugems/gpugems2/part-v-image-oriented-computing/chapter-42-conservative-rasterization .
We use reversed-Z far depths and full-cell underestimated triangle coverage,
then overestimated transformed bounds. Unlike a center-sample depth test this
cannot hide an object through an uncovered portion of a cell. Current camera
and current transforms rebuild depth each frame; no previous query result is
trusted. Near-plane-crossing triangles do not occlude. Shared triangle edges
can leave conservative holes, causing extra draws, never missing surfaces.
Babylon's public WebGL2 support description establishes the rival behaviour:
https://doc.babylonjs.com/setup/support/webGL2/ . Both implementations suppress
opaque meshes behind other opaque surfaces. Margo takes the CPU-depth option
explicitly allowed by the job, avoiding asynchronous query latency. No rival
source or companion repository was read or copied.

### Batch 243 learned denoiser (2026-11-09)
Research compared: Steve Bako et al., *Kernel-Predicting Convolutional Networks for Denoising Monte Carlo Renderings* (2017), https://jannovak.info/publications/KPCN/index.html; Thijs Vogels et al., *Denoising with Kernel Prediction and Asymmetric Loss Functions* (2018), https://jannovak.info/publications/KPAL/index.html; Jaakko Lehtinen et al., *Noise2Noise: Learning Image Restoration without Clean Data* (2018), https://proceedings.mlr.press/v80/lehtinen18a.html. No companion code, foreign model or training dataset was used.
A repository-authored 10->16->8->1 MLP scores nine neighbors, followed by positive normalized kernel reconstruction. Inputs are spatial offset, HDR-normalized color difference and variance, albedo difference, normal agreement, tone-mapped center/neighbor luminance, coverage difference, inverse square-root sample count and radius conditioning. Supervised targets come from authored analytic patch families with albedo/normal boundaries, lighting changes, highlights and coverage. Independent training/validation seeds are 24301/24302, 24000/4000 patches, 800 Adam steps. Variance is augmented independently of sample count with log noise power [-8,0]; variance-balanced normalized MSE prevents over-blurring low-variance MIS/area-light input. This repaired an observed real-image regression: the original fixed-variance training increased the Box holdout MSE from 0.0002043207 to 0.0003075558. Balanced training lowers it to 0.0001771820, under the same strict improvement assertion. Training script, final weight hash, NumPy version and validation report are retained in the package tests.
The GPU holdout reuses the unmodified Khronos metadata Box fixture (CC-BY-4.0, The Khronos Group), already recorded in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md and packages/gltf/test/fixtures/metadata/NOTICE.md. Its scene/camera/light/sample seeds are absent from training. Compatibility reconstructs exactly the same native-produced raw image and AOVs, avoiding a second renderer as an uncontrolled input difference.

## Batch 224 job 4: mesh hulls and nonconvex Minkowski sums
Compared C. Bradford Barber, David P. Dobkin and Hannu Huhdanpaa, The Quickhull Algorithm for Convex Hulls (1996), https://www.wias-berlin.de/people/si/course/files/Barber96-quickhull.pdf; Bernard Chazelle, David P. Dobkin, Nadia Shouraboura and Ayellet Tal, Strategies for Polyhedral Surface Decomposition: An Experimental Study (1997), https://www.ee.technion.ac.il/~ayellet/Ps/decomp-97.pdf; Peter Hachenberger, Exact Minkowski Sums of Polyhedra and Exact and Efficient Decomposition of Polyhedra in Convex Pieces (2007), https://research.tue.nl/files/1835753/Metis212139.pdf; Gilbert Bernstein and Don Fussell, Fast, Exact, Linear Booleans (2009), https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-8659.2009.01504.x; and Manifold contributors, Hull and MinkowskiSum API descriptions (2026), https://manifoldcad.org/docs/html/classmanifold_1_1_manifold.html. No companion or rival source was read or copied. The outside CAD API inspection from job 1 applies; no outside kernel is imported.
Combined design: geometry/hull exposes original-point triangle indices from the existing Quickhull implementation, with translated unit-frame predicates and empty lower-dimensional output. The original convexGeometry API retains its old behavior and float32 drawing buffers. mesh-edit/hull compacts source double positions into editable triangles and planar UVs. For Minkowski, exact BSP interior cells are bounded by source planes and the source box; three-plane meets and containment predicates stay in the existing exact space until cell export. A convex input skips enumeration entirely. Each convex pair sums all vertex pairs and hulls them, then the existing batch boolean unions every result in one exact space. This follows the set identity (union Ai) + (union Bj) = union(Ai + Bj); it preserves concavity, components and cavities instead of convexifying the final sum. Reflex-edge decomposition could use fewer cells, but BSP reuses the established owned predicates and exposes cell/pair/triple budgets. No minimum-decomposition or elapsed-time claim is made.
Rule 24 geometry gap: convexGeometry narrows positions to float32, which loses a unit cube at offset 1e9. The new optional geometry/hull source-index API keeps that conversion out of topology work, rather than copying the hull algorithm into mesh-edit. The existing numeric implementations are reused, with no measured Wasm gain or new runtime dependency. No core/stage changes, external demo assets, registry package or foreign files. Evidence: geometry/tests/hull-indices.test.js and unchanged convex tests; mesh-edit/tests/hull.test.js proves analytic convex, L-shape, two-nonconvex, cavity and disconnected sums, translation covariance, work limits, ownership and cancellation. Native and compatibility rendering checks draw the result.

algorithm, triangulation or evaluator was replaced, no rival source or companion code was read,
and no speed claim is made. Existing geometry code does the same deterministic work.

The downstream PBR per-primitive bound is retained. FBX partitions large materials at whole-triangle boundaries instead of raising the GPU storage-binding bound: W3C GPU for the Web Working Group, *WebGPU* (2026 living specification), https://www.w3.org/TR/webgpu/#dom-supported-limits-maxstoragebufferbindingsize . Existing public GLTFAsset/PBRModel and prepareGLTF APIs receive the configured byte/node caps; no missing glTF API or core change was needed.

## Batch 172 job 4: finite-element probes and integrals
- Jonathan Richard Shewchuk, "What Is a Good Linear Finite Element? Interpolation, Conditioning, Anisotropy, and Quality Measures", 2002, https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~jrs/papers/elemj.pdf . Barycentric affine interpolation, physical simplex measures and conditioning limits. Margo uses analytic simplex measures and explicitly states membership/conditioning limits instead of claiming exact predicates.
- NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, "Section 3.5: Quadrature", edited by F. W. J. Olver et al., current 2026 edition, https://dlmf.nist.gov/3.5 . Gaussian polynomial exactness supports the three-node tensor rule for a nonfolded trilinear hexahedron's polynomial field times Jacobian product. Simplex field integration instead uses exact barycentric means; these approaches are combined by cell type.
- Kitware, "VTK 9.5 Release Details: vtkIntegrateAttributes integration strategies", 2025, https://docs.vtk.org/en/v9.5.0/release_details/9.5.html . Behavioral reference for separating Gaussian integration from triangulation-based field integration. The probe entry states explicitly which field model each cell type uses.
- NASA TMR FUN3D SA slice and the OpenNeuro ds000030 UCLA CNP T1 already attributed in this repository provide the real-data demonstrations. Only repository data and public mathematical descriptions were used; no rival or companion source was read. Uniform coordinate buckets narrow cell candidates; the implementation does not claim a ray-traversal algorithm or a measured Rust/Wasm gain.

## Batch 223: oriented boxes on all culling lists

Gil Gribb and Klaus Hartmann, *Fast Extraction of Viewing Frustum Planes from the
World-View-Projection Matrix*, 2001,
https://scottfielder.com/Literature/fast-extraction-viewing-frustum-planes-from-world-view-projection-matrix.pdf ,
and Stefan Gottschalk, Ming C. Lin and Dinesh Manocha, *OBBTree: A Hierarchical
Structure for Rapid Interference Detection*, SIGGRAPH 1996,
https://techreports.cs.unc.edu/papers/96-013.pdf , motivate plane tests using the
support radius of a transformed box. Compared with a sphere this retains actual
axis extents under rotation, reflection, nonuniform scale and shear. Combine it
with Greene, Kass and Miller (1993), cited above, for depth bounds: projected
corners give conservative screen and near-depth intervals. We expand each clip
coordinate by transformed world-error bounds before division, so padding stays
conservative under oblique transforms too. Sphere size cuts remain unchanged.
The optional subclass owns all box mathematics; ordinary cullers only dispatch
an optional package-local shape hook. Tests use the existing attributed Cesium
Box sample, scaled into rods. No rival source or companion implementation used.

The software occluder now removes an internal diagonal only for an exactly
coplanar convex triangle pair with consistent winding. This applies the
inessential-diagonal principle described by Stefan Hertel and Kurt Mehlhorn,
*Fast triangulation of the plane with respect to simple polygons*, 1985
(expanding their 1983 paper), https://doi.org/10.1016/S0019-9958(85)80044-9 ,
compared with Bernard Chazelle and David P. Dobkin, *Optimal Convex
Decompositions*, 1985,
https://www.cs.princeton.edu/~chazelle/pubs/OptimalConvexDecomp.pdf .
We need safe convex patches, not a minimum decomposition, so a linear adjacency
pass only joins pairs. Exact float32 dyadic integer predicates verify
coplanarity and convexity before removing a diagonal. Folded, concave and
oppositely wound pairs stay separate. Cached patches compare snapshots so
mutable public software geometry refreshes them. Inner full-cell coverage and
far-depth bounds still apply to every patch; no corner-only sampling shortcut
was introduced. Regression tests cover seams and actual concave gaps.

## Batch 232 textured moon (2026-11-10)

Clean-room implementation in `packages/sky/src/moon.ts`, with no rival code read.
Sources compared: P. K. Seidelmann et al., *Report of the IAU/IAG Working Group on
cartographic coordinates and rotational elements: 2006* (2007),
https://doi.org/10.1007/s10569-007-9072-y; Ernie Wright and Noah Petro,
*CGI Moon Kit* (NASA SVS, 2019, updated 2026), https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/4720/;
Rodrigo Luger, Eric Agol, Fran Bartolic and Daniel Foreman-Mackey,
*Analytic Light Curves in Reflected Light: Phase Curves, Occultations, and
Non-Lambertian Scattering for Spherical Planets and Moons* (2021),
https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.06275; Peter Thejll et al., *On the colour of the dark
side of the Moon* (2014), https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.1994.
The mean Earth/polar axis convention fixes the centre at longitude/latitude 0;
NASA supplies north-first, zero-centred equirectangular data. Spherical ray
intersection supplies the terminator, Lambert illumination supplies sunlight and
the complementary Earth phase, and a modest blue earthlight tint follows Thejll's
qualitative observation. This is a visual model, not a calibrated lunar BRDF or
ephemeris: no libration, terrain relief, atmospheric extinction or eclipses.
The caller supplies lunar direction and north in world coordinates. Orientation
is independent of camera roll. No internet or global state is touched on import.

release, rather than relying on page navigation and garbage collection.

## Batch 223: stable ordering after compaction

Kenneth E. Batcher, *Sorting Networks and Their Applications*, AFIPS 1968,
https://doi.org/10.1145/1468075.1468121 , gives the deterministic compare-exchange
schedule used by the optional /sort entry. Peter Kipfer and Rudiger Westermann,
*Improved GPU Sorting*, GPU Gems 2, 2005,
https://developer.nvidia.com/gpugems/gpugems2/part-vi-simulation-and-numerical-algorithms/chapter-46-improved-gpu-sorting ,
compares GPU sorting networks and describes their use for view-depth ordering.
We combine that schedule with the opaque front-to-back visibility rationale of
Greene, Kass and Miller (1993), cited above. Each live key includes its original
row index, making equal depths stable. Invalid padded lanes sort last. The
network sorts only keys, then gathers entire original 96-byte rows. Each stage
has its own 256-byte uniform slot; each view has separate keys, parameters and
outputs, so queue writes cannot replace another stage's or view's data before
submission. All original indices, material/tint/UV fields and count words stay.
No rival or paper companion code was consulted. The new tests use the existing
licensed Cesium Box sample and independent CPU ordering of direct GPU readbacks.

### Batch 222: cluster LOD and compatibility readback tasks (2026-11-10)
Research compared Hugues Hoppe, *View-dependent refinement of progressive meshes* (SIGGRAPH 1997), https://hhoppe.com/proj/vdrpm/ (local refinement and projected geometric error); Michael Garland and Paul Heckbert, *Surface Simplification Using Quadric Error Metrics* (SIGGRAPH 1997), https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~garland/quadrics/ (vertex-subset quadric collapse); Brian Karis, Rune Stubbe and Graham Wihlidal, *A Deep Dive into Nanite Virtualized Geometry* (SIGGRAPH 2021), https://advances.realtimerendering.com/s2021/index.html (meshlet hierarchy and boundary constraints). Combined spatial region partitioning, boundary-pinned simplification and an adaptive error cut; no engine or companion source read or copied. The separate private tooling workspace was inspected first; its supported package surfaces do not supply a meshlet/simplification entry that fits this optional web rendering feature. No files or implementation were imported from it.
The optional cluster builder delegates collapse to mesh-edit/modeling. Its additive lockedVertices option forbids moving a pinned vertex. maxDeviation accumulates endpoint displacement radii through each collapse, unlike a quadric's squared plane cost. Parent errors add that displacement bound to the maximum child error. Every region boundary is pinned, including split-normal edges; leaves retain every original triangle. Parent approximations are repacked into bounded meshlets. A shared screen-noise interval partitions each root-to-leaf path, so selection can cross-fade continuously with independently chosen regions. This is a CPU-selected spatial tree, not a claim of Nanite's GPU throughput, streaming or software rasterization. Native and full compatibility execute the same optional WGSL patch; core and stage do not change.
For the LOD imposter wait, compared WHATWG contributors, *HTML Living Standard: Timers* and *Web messaging* (2026), https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/timers-and-user-prompts.html and https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/web-messaging.html; W3C GPU for the Web Working Group, *WebGPU* (2026), https://www.w3.org/TR/webgpu/; Khronos Group, *OpenGL ES 3.0 API reference* (2012), https://www.khronos.org/files/opengles3-quick-reference-card.pdf. Fence and query readiness still require a later browser task; using a delayed scheduler task (a message task followed by a fresh timer on browsers without Scheduler) removes inherited timer clamping while leaving the main loop idle for fence status to advance. Buffer mapping drains pending submissions and polls its own nonforcing readback readiness instead of adding a second device-wide fence; GPU-only invalid shadows still use the queue fence. There is no blocking finish, changed picking grid or relaxed assertion. Tests forbid timers while executing actual fence/map methods through many serial completions, preserve pending-submit ordering and reject device loss.
The browser demonstration uses the existing FlightHelmet mobile asset, Gary Hsu / Microsoft, CC0-1.0, source and derivation in examples/assets/ATTRIBUTION.md and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md. No new third-party asset or runtime dependency. No speed benchmark was run.
Additional readiness research: WICG contributors, *Prioritized Task Scheduling* (2026), https://wicg.github.io/scheduling-apis/; Khronos Group, *WebGL 2.0 Specification*, sync objects (2026 living specification), https://registry.khronos.org/webgl/specs/latest/2.0/ . WebGL only advances a new sync object's signaled state outside an executing task. Immediate message-task polling generated millions of readiness queries in the unchanged picking diagnostic, so the final helper leaves an explicit idle interval instead. No elapsed-time performance claim is published. The hierarchy's real-asset regression also exposed a second boundary constraint: a collapse must not create a previously absent edge between two pinned vertices, since it can collide with an independently simplified neighboring region after the regions are joined. The collapse check now preserves that interface graph as well as every boundary position.
Batch 222 validation also refreshed the compatibility corpus with the actual GPU-compiled labels shader introduced on current main, closing the existing package-coverage check without weakening it or running dependent GPU suites. The source is Margo's packages/labels/src/gpu-shader.ts; existing check:wgsl --packages=labels reproduces its compile. The corpus's hashes and all previous modules remain checked. Cluster renderer disposal leaves later registered passes inert, covered by a CPU lifetime regression. Its real-asset GPU harness captures the canvas in the render task, as required by WebGPU presentation, and retains the original pixel assertions. Native and compatibility produce identical cuts (5686 near triangles, 4734 at the 16 pixel budget) and 2068/2102 shared lit pixels. These are deterministic work and image counts, not a speed measurement.

### KB5339c: Blender Elastic easing, fitted black box (2026-11-11)
Sources: Robert Penner, *Robert Penner's Programming Macromedia Flash MX*, chapter 7, Motion, Tweening, and Easing (2002), and the easing equations as he published them at http://robertpenner.com/easing/ (easeInElastic, easeOutElastic, easeInOutElastic with amplitude a, period p, default p = 0.3 d, or 0.45 d for in-out, and s = p / (2 pi) asin(c / a), or a = c and s = p / 4 when a < |c|); Blender Foundation, *Blender Manual*, F-Curve properties, Active Keyframe panel (4.2), https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/4.2/editors/graph_editor/fcurves/properties.html , and F-Curve introduction, Interpolation Mode (2.93), https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/2.93/editors/graph_editor/fcurves/introduction.html (search extracts; full fetch returned 403): Elastic overshoots, rebounds and settles with decreasing intensity, Amplitude sets how far it overshoots, Period sets how often it oscillates. No Blender source was read, and the curve was not written from any recollection of how Blender implements it: every term below was established from measurements alone, and the model was accepted only because it reproduces them.
Measured: Blender 5.3.0 Beta `fcurve.evaluate` on two-key Elastic spans, run as a black box. 84 cases (4 easings x 7 amplitude/period pairs x 3 key pairs, 65 sub-frame samples), then 176 dense cases (401 samples: amplitude 0 to 3 against change 0.5 to 2 of both signs, periods 0 to 30, spans 7 to 80 frames), 33 edge cases (equal keys, negative amplitude and period, half-frame span, period 0.5, amplitude 0.999 and 1e6) and 108 negative-period cases. Penner's equations as published miss by up to 4.3.
Derivation, each step read off the data: (1) Ease-out equals the point mirror of Blender's own ease-in, out(t) = b + c - (in(d - t) - b), in all 21 key and setting pairs to 1.2e-7; AUTO equals ease-out exactly. In-out is point symmetric about its middle, which sits at b + c / 2. So only ease-in and in-out's first half need a form. (2) Ease-in with amplitude a >= |c| equals Penner's easeInElastic to float error, both signs of c. (3) For a < |c| the miss from Penner's a = c branch grows exactly linearly in |c| - a (0.3731, 0.2798, 0.1865, 0.0373 at a = 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.9, c = 1). (4) At a = 0 the curve is b until s = p / 4 frames before the end key (first non-zero sample at 37 for p = 12, 39 for p = 4, 32.6 for p = 30, 74 for d = 80 with the default p = 24), and inside that window the ratio to Penner's a = c curve is 1 - (d - t) / s to 1e-6 in every case. (5) Steps 3 and 4 combine into one scale on Penner's a = c curve, r + (1 - r) w with r = a / |c| and w = clamp(1 - (d - t) / s, 0, 1); equal keys with a = 0 stay flat. (6) In-out: a least-squares fit of the first half to -A 2^(10u) sin((u d - S) 2 pi / p), u = 2t / d - 1, gives A = a / 2 and sin(2 pi S / p) = c / a for a > |c|, A = c / 2 and S = p / 4 at a = |c|, with the window of step 4 measured in the same doubled time (first non-zero 2.25, 0.75 and 1.875 frames before the middle for p = 18, 6, 15). So the first half is b + in(2t) / 2 with the in-out default period 0.45 d. (7) A negative period: Blender keeps it (a negative amplitude it stores as 0). With a > |c| Penner's formula with the signed p fits; with a < |c| the oscillation term sin(2 pi u d / p - pi / 2) is even in p, and the window is |p| / 4 long. Using the signed p with a window of |s| fits both.
Fit: all 401 measured cases, 122,497 samples, agree within Blender's single-precision rounding: at most 1.6e-5 of max(1, |value|, amplitude x 2^(10(x - 1))), where the worst points are the steepest samples (period 0.5 or 4 frames near the end key; amplitude 1e6 near a zero of the sine), which is the error of rounding the frame time and the sine argument to 32 bits times the local slope: evaluated at the float32-rounded frame, the model stays within 0.41 of a bound of one float32 step of the frame times the local slope plus four steps of the value in every case but amplitude 1e6, whose largest miss, 0.39 on a swing of 8.7e5, is 4.5e-7 of it. Times and periods enter only as t / d and p / d (spans of 7, 20, 40, 80 and 100 frames agree), so the exporter writes the period in seconds. Regression: `packages/blender/tests/nodes.test.js` (KB5339c) pins 135 of these cases from `packages/blender/tests/fixtures/elastic-probe.json`, written by `tools/blender-addon/tests/blender_elastic.py`.
### KB5339d: Blender F-curve Noise modifier, carried as Blender's own samples (2026-11-11)

Problem: a live-node socket F-curve with a Noise modifier kept frame samples and was interpolated linearly, so a seek between frames missed Blender (up to 0.078 on the fixture). Blender's noise hash is not in a published description, an integer hash cannot be fitted from samples like a smooth curve, and reading Blender's source to reimplement it is barred by the clean-room rule. Coordinator's ruling: carry the values, not the model.

Method: the add-on calls Blender's documented Python API inside Blender, `FCurve.evaluate(frame)` (Blender Python API reference, bpy.types.FCurve, https://docs.blender.org/api/current/bpy.types.FCurve.html), which applies the curve's modifiers; measured against the scene's evaluated socket value at eighth-frame steps it agreed exactly (0 difference) on a Noise curve. The sample step is an eighth of a frame, halved while the finest noise octave, `scale / lacunarity^depth` frames (bpy.types.FModifierNoise, https://docs.blender.org/api/current/bpy.types.FModifierNoise.html), is shorter than 8 steps, down to 1/1024 frame; steps are powers of two so every key time is exact in binary and every eighth frame is a sampled step. Samples become LINEAR keys, then a greedy pass keeps a sample only when linear interpolation from the last kept key cannot give back every sample in between within one float32 step (IEEE 754-2019, binary32). The pass grows each span with the slope-cone test of swinging-door trending (E. H. Bristol, "Swinging Door Trending: Adaptive Trend Recording?", ISA National Conference Proceedings, 1990) and confirms it with the reader's own double-precision formula. Compared: Douglas and Peucker's split method (D. H. Douglas, T. K. Peucker, "Algorithms for the reduction of the number of points required to represent a digitized line or its caricature", Cartographica 10(2), 1973, https://doi.org/10.3138/FM57-6770-U75U-7727) bounds the error but not the key count; Imai and Iri's shortest path over feasible spans (H. Imai, M. Iri, "Polygonal approximation of a curve: formulations and algorithms", Computational Morphology, North-Holland, 1988) gives the minimum key count at quadratic cost. The greedy pass is linear in practice and reaches the minimum when feasible spans nest; it is not proven minimal in general. On the fixture, the ramp outside a restricted noise range reduces 385 samples to 207 keys; unrestricted noise keeps every sample.

Result: at every sampled step the reader gives Blender's value within one float32 step (exact on 3 of 4 noise channels); between steps, at most 5.9e-4 off (docs/limits.md). Regression: `packages/blender/tests/nodes.test.js` (KB5339d) on `packages/blender/tests/fixtures/node-noise.json`, written by `tools/blender-addon/tests/blender_node_noise.py`, which fails on the old export.

### Batch 247 job 2: painted interreflection and exact temporal reuse
Combined Cindy M. Goral, Kenneth E. Torrance, Donald P. Greenberg and Bennett Battaile, *Modeling the Interaction of Light Between Diffuse Surfaces* (1984), https://courses.washington.edu/arch481/00HomePage/4.Miscellaneous/0.Handouts/1984.radiosity.siggraph.pdf ; Gregory J. Ward, Francis M. Rubinstein and Robert D. Clear, *A Ray Tracing Solution for Diffuse Interreflection* (1988), https://radsite.lbl.gov/radiance/papers/index.html ; Marco Salvi, *An Excursion in Temporal Supersampling* (2016), https://developer.download.nvidia.com/gameworks/events/GDC2016/msalvi_temporal_supersampling.pdf ; and the Osborne/Sannikov 2024 and Freeman/Sannikov/Margel 2025 radiance-cascade papers cited above. Painted cells retain separate outward-face radiance, gather the previous finite bounce order with the same normalized cosine quadrature as analytic patches, and modulate by painted linear albedo. Opaque nearest-hit ordering combines emission with that face's reflection. Internal faces are inactive.
Ward motivates reuse of computed indirect values; Salvi identifies invalid history under lighting changes and disocclusion. This implementation uses exact input equality instead of approximate clipping/averaging: analytic/configuration snapshots on CPU and complete RGBA source/emission comparisons on GPU invalidate all affected surface/probe history immediately. No stochastic reprojection or temporal lag is introduced. Immutable zero-order input is separate from persistent ping-pong outputs. Multiple passes share one painted snapshot per encoder. A moving camera rebuilds; static frames skip interval tracing. Deterministic evidence is cached GPU buffers remaining untouched on an unchanged frame and rebuilding on reset/disable. No measured speed number. John Amanatides and Andrew Woo, *A Fast Voxel Traversal Algorithm for Ray Tracing* (1987), https://www.cse.yorku.ca/~amana/research/grid.pdf , supplies the cell-boundary traversal reference used with the exact distance bound. No companion/rival source was read or copied.

## Batch 240 job 1: data-driven voxel box models (2026-11-10)

Clean-room design compares grid traversal, slab intersections, exact box boundary extraction and documented web voxel model behaviour. No rival or companion source was read or imported. Existing private tooling was inspected first; this raster/query feature uses only existing engine packages.

- John Amanatides and Andrew Woo, 1987, *A Fast Voxel Traversal Algorithm for Ray Tracing*, Eurographics: https://www.cs.yorku.ca/~amana/research/grid.pdf . Retain the package's cell DDA and intersect each prepared box only within that cell's interval.
- Amy Williams, Steve Barrus, R. Keith Morley and Peter Shirley, 2005, *An Efficient and Robust Ray-Box Intersection Algorithm*, Journal of Graphics Tools 10(1), 55-60: https://doi.org/10.1080/2151237X.2005.10129188 . Slab interval clipping, explicit parallel axes, half-open box boundaries, no zero-volume tangency hits.
- Samuli Laine and Tero Karras, 2010, *Efficient Sparse Voxel Octrees*, I3D: https://research.nvidia.com/publication/2010-02_efficient-sparse-voxel-octrees . Compared coarse occupancy against detailed contours: retain exact boxes rather than reducing custom models to the slab/stair octant mask. No octree implementation is used here.
- Voxelize authors, 2026, *Custom Blocks*: https://docs.voxelize.io/tutorials/intermediate/custom-blocks . Public behaviour comparison: box lists, per-face textures, rotation, light emitters and collision are present. This job provides these for exact axis-aligned box unions, including 24 cube orientations. Its test fixtures are original mathematical data, not downloaded demo art.

Box union surfaces are derived by subtracting intersecting rectangles at each box face. Precompute all proper signed axis permutations, their UV correspondences and exact full-face light masks at definition. Rendering uses the existing optional materials pipeline with per-face texture callbacks; picking, character sweeps, scalar/worker/RGB light and solver triangle colliders share the prepared boxes. No wall-clock gain, arbitrary-angle box rotation or new core capability is claimed.
- Batch 213 pose tracking: landmark topology, quaternion-frame method and smoothing alternatives researched and compared in [rigging-pose-tracking](rigging-pose-tracking.md#clean-room-sources). Opaque Kalidokit 1.1.5 outputs recorded from external engine-bench; no rival source or files copied.
## Batch 235 job 1: local water ripples (2026-11-10)

Research compared Michael Kass and Gavin Miller, Rapid, stable fluid dynamics for computer graphics (1990), https://doi.org/10.1145/97880.97884 ; Matthias Mueller, How to write a Water Simulator (2022), https://matthias-research.github.io/pages/tenMinutePhysics/20-heightFieldWater.pdf ; Nuttapong Chentanez and Matthias Mueller, Real-time Simulation of Large Bodies of Water with Small Scale Details (2010), https://matthias-research.github.io/pages/publications/hfFluid.pdf ; and Stefan Jeschke and Chris Wojtan, Generalizing Shallow Water Simulations with Dispersive Surface Waves (2023), https://research.nvidia.com/labs/prl/shallow-water-simulation/ . The first two motivate the height/velocity stencil and stable substeps; the 2010 paper motivates finite absorbing borders and separate small waves. The 2023 paper explains why these local constant-speed disturbances must not claim full dispersive coupling. Combine those descriptions with Margo-authored compact swept disturbances and integer world-preserving scroll. Only papers were read, never companion or rival code. See water-ripples.md.
### Batch 222 job 3: complementary imposter fades (2026-11-10)
Compared Jorge Jimenez, *Next Generation Post Processing in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare* (SIGGRAPH 2014), https://www.iryoku.com/next-generation-post-processing-in-call-of-duty-advanced-warfare/ ; Eric Enderton, Erik Sintorn, Peter Shirley and David Luebke, *Stochastic Transparency* (I3D 2010, TVCG 2011), https://www.luebke.us/publications/StochasticTransparency_I3D2010.pdf and https://doi.org/10.1109/TVCG.2010.123 ; W3C GPU for the Web Working Group, *WebGPU* (2026 working draft), https://www.w3.org/TR/webgpu/ . The shared IGN threshold follows Jimenez; complementary coverage is motivated by screen-door/stochastic coverage, without claiming Enderton's accumulation algorithm. Existing Margo mesh fading and imposter WGSL are combined clean room, with no companion or rival source read. The unused color.w instance component carries a signed fade value, keeping the 24-float record and existing resource bindings. Derivatives execute before the new discard. Native WebGPU and full compatibility compile the same shader.
The real CC0 FlightHelmet regression renders mesh-to-static, static-to-animated, animated-to-mesh and imposter-to-null dissolves. Shared first-frame tests exposed an existing atlas ownership defect: matching only an image aliased sequence ranges and playback rates. Atlas reuse now includes sequence identity, proven by distinct 2/7 fps sequences sharing both images. No benchmark or speed claim.
Batch 222 job 3 validation uses the existing shared hiddenInTree helper rather than duplicating ancestor traversal. W3C WebGPU queue completion semantics above also govern the outline fixture: synchronize submitted selection/compute work before a fresh same-task canvas capture, so lazy compatibility compute initialization is included in the proof. No extra frame-count or time-based readiness assumption is introduced.


## Batch 198 job 1: configurable view cube frame (2026-11-10)
Compared Azam Khan, Igor Mordatch, George Fitzmaurice, Justin Matejka and Gordon Kurtenbach, *ViewCube: A 3D Orientation Indicator and Controller* (I3D 2008), https://damassets.autodesk.net/content/dam/autodesk/www/autodesk-reasearch/Publications/pdf/viewcube-a-3d-orientation.pdf ; Tom Duff, James Burgess, Per Christensen, Christophe Hery, Andrew Kensler, Max Liani and Ryusuke Villemin, *Building an Orthonormal Basis, Revisited* (JCGT 2017), https://jcgt.org/published/0006/01/01/ ; and xeokit SDK contributors, *NavCubePlugin API reference* (accessed 2026-11-10), https://xeokit.github.io/xeokit-sdk/docs/class/src/plugins/NavCubePlugin/NavCubePlugin.js~NavCubePlugin.html . Read paper descriptions and API documentation only, never companion or rival implementation code. Khan supplies the consistent global-up navigation model; Duff motivates explicit orthogonality and singularity tests. We project a user front hint onto the up plane, normalize it, and derive right by a cross product. This deliberately preserves a caller's front instead of using a single-vector basis algorithm that chooses an arbitrary heading. The optional UpViewCube maps existing navigation and CSS display through inverse orthonormal transforms, so face, edge, corner, keyboard, drag, home and roll share one frame. Tests cover both poles, negative and oblique up, custom front, inverse mapping and invalid input. The small protected frame hooks live in viewcube, not core or stage. No external asset or demo was added; browser fixtures are original analytic geometry.

The job also repairs CameraProjection's fixed-Y pole test: its singularity test now uses worldUp cross view, and the optional cube supplies its frame's -front as pole screen up. Regression: packages/cameras/test/world-up.test.js plus the cube/projection integration test. Existing default Y-up behavior stays the same. Compared the geometric projection and world-frame descriptions above with Matt Pharr, Wenzel Jakob and Greg Humphreys, Physically Based Rendering, fourth edition, section 5.2 Projective Camera Models (2023), https://www.pbr-book.org/4ed/Cameras_and_Film/Projective_Camera_Models . Only the geometric descriptions were used; no code from the accompanying book implementation was copied or adapted.

## Batch 201 job 1: spec/gloss to metal/rough (2026-11-10)
Compared Saurabh Bhatia, Gary Hsu and Patrick Cozzi for Khronos, *KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness* (2017, archived specification), https://github.com/KhronosGroup/glTF/tree/main/extensions/2.0/Archived/KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness ; Brent Burley, *Physically-Based Shading at Disney* (2012), https://disneyanimation.com/publications/physically-based-shading-at-disney/ ; Bruce Walter, Stephen R. Marschner, Hongsong Li and Kenneth E. Torrance, *Microfacet Models for Refraction through Rough Surfaces* (2007), https://www.cs.cornell.edu/~srm/publications/EGSR07-btdf.pdf ; and the Khronos 3D Formats Working Group, *glTF 2.0 Specification*, material model and BRDF appendix (2026 retrieval), https://registry.khronos.org/glTF/specs/2.0/glTF-2.0.html . Public rival behavior: Babylon.js GLTFFileLoader's documented KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness option, https://doc.babylonjs.com/typedoc/classes/BABYLON.GLTFFileLoader . Read papers, specifications and documentation only, never rival or companion implementation code.
The combination routes the authored workflow during loading, solves a metalness quadratic from diffuse energy and F0, blends diffuse/specular base-colour estimates and uses roughness = 1 - gloss. Textured conversion runs after independent sRGB sampling and filtering, so unrelated UV sets, transforms and samplers stay intact without texture baking. This is a metal/rough approximation for arbitrary coloured dielectrics, not an exact representation of every spec/gloss BRDF. Numeric endpoint and independent GPU reference checks cover the conversion; the real Microsoft/Khronos sample renders on both backends. The CPU helper and WGSL were written clean room from these material descriptions and algebra. No speed claim.


## Batch 242 job 1: rooms and lobby (2026-11-10)
Research compared Ashwin Bharambe, Jeffrey Pang and Srinivasan Seshan, A Distributed Architecture for Online Multiplayer Games (NSDI 2006), https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~srini/papers/papers/2006-Bharambe-nsdi/2006-Bharambe-nsdi.pdf (authoritative ownership and independent state); Hugo Krawczyk, Mihir Bellare and Ran Canetti, HMAC: Keyed-Hashing for Message Authentication (RFC 2104, 1997), https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2104.html (authenticated claims); and Colyseus contributors, Rooms and Matchmaking (2026 retrieval), https://docs.colyseus.io/room and https://docs.colyseus.io/matchmaker (public behavioral contract, no source). Combine independent authoritative VoxelServers, synchronous seat reservation before asynchronous signing, and the existing HMAC-SHA-256 shard ticket format. The room owns nonce consumption and capacity, including disconnected players retained for resume. Tests show the requested rival behaviors: independent worlds, join-by-code, listing, capacity with concurrent requests, expiring reservations and join-or-create. This is a single-process lobby, not the research paper's distributed replication system. No rival or companion source, external asset or demo was added.

### Batch 214 job 2: limit-aware swivel
Compared Andreas Aristidou, Yiorgos Chrysanthou and Joan Lasenby, Extending FABRIK with Model Constraints (2015 online, 2016 volume), https://doi.org/10.1002/cav.1630; F. Sebastian Grassia, Practical Parameterization of Rotations Using the Exponential Map (1998), https://doi.org/10.1080/10867651.1998.10487493; and Ben Kenwright, Inverse Kinematics with Dual-Quaternions, Exponential-Maps, and Joint Limits (2022), https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.01466. ## Batch 173 job 2: label and multi-component volume fusion
Research compared categorical versus continuous interpolation, post-classification mixture rules, registration without resampling, and optical-depth compositing before implementation. Sources read were publications/API prose only, never companion code or rival implementation files:
- Nelson Max, *Optical Models for Direct Volume Rendering* (1995), IEEE TVCG 1(2), https://doi.org/10.1109/2945.468400. Combine extinction in optical depth and correct opacity for travelled voxel distance.
- Ralph Brecheisen, Anna Vilanova i Bartroli, Bram Platel and Bart ter Haar Romeny, *Flexible GPU-Based Multi-Volume Ray-Casting* (2008), VMV, https://graphics.tudelft.nl/Publications-new/2008/BVPH08a/pdf.pdf. Paper read through TU Delft's publications PDF index. It compares sample-level mixing strategies and independent source transforms. We use a common ray, independent inverse affine mappings and optical/over/maximum mixing. No depth-peeling implementation is copied or claimed.
- Stefan Lindholm and Alexander Bock, *Poor Man's Rendering Of Segmented Data* (2013), SIGRAD pp.49-54, https://ep.liu.se/ecp/094/007/ecp13094007.pdf. It explains why interpolating integer class IDs creates absent classes. We retain nearest integer lookup and explicit neighbouring-category comparisons, rather than its filtered-label shortcut. IDs are losslessly remapped to dense GPU indices; unknown categories retain distinct boundary IDs and transparent classification.
- Kitware, *vtk.js VolumeProperty API* (accessed 2026-11-10), https://kitware.github.io/vtk-js/api/Rendering_Core_VolumeProperty.html. Prose contract compared: independent components/weights, RGB/RGBA, label colour/opacity and per-category pixel outlines. Our outline kernel compares eight pixel neighbours at each thickness radius in the ray-perpendicular screen footprint. No source links followed.
- Michela Antonelli et al., *The Medical Segmentation Decathlon* (2022), Nature Communications 13:4128, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-30695-9; https://medicaldecathlon.com/dataaws/. Demo uses original BRATS_457 intensity/label samples at strides 4,4,4; dataset.json explicitly CC BY-SA 4.0. Source/output hashes, modalities, category names, affine and changes are recorded in examples/assets/sciviz/msd-brain.json. The existing OpenNeuro T1 remains CC0. No scientific or clinical accuracy, speed or general engine superiority claim.


## Batch 203: shared JPEG decoding (2026-11-10)

The existing Margo exporter JPEG reader is now the single implementation in
packages/shared/jpeg.js, with typed optional entries in decoders/jpeg and
exporters/jpeg-read. No external implementation was read or copied.
Research compared Gregory K. Wallace, "The JPEG Still Picture Compression
Standard" (1991, https://ijg.org/files/Wallace.JPEG.pdf), the overview of DCT
and coding modes; CCITT Study Group VIII and ISO/IEC JTC1/SC29/WG1,
"T.81: Digital compression and coding of continuous-tone still images"
(1992, https://www.w3.org/Graphics/JPEG/itu-t81.pdf), annexes C, F and G for
Huffman, sequential and progressive scans; and ITU-T, "T.871: JPEG File
Interchange Format" (2011, https://www.itu.int/rec/T-REC-T.871/en), for
YCbCr and centered chroma. T.81 determines the byte grammar, Wallace explains
the transform and mode distinction, and T.871 supplies the color convention.
This move preserves the algorithm and its independent libjpeg-turbo bounds.
The ten exporter JPEG/reference PNG pairs cover baseline, progressive,
restart, optimized tables, RGB and grayscale. They are Margo generated data,
documented in packages/exporters/tests/fixtures/NOTICE.md. The new decoder
tests compare those same references, exercise image dispatch and pixel
limits, and decode a progressive file in a Node worker without image APIs.
No new CPU loop, Wasm claim or timing claim is introduced.

## Batch 242 job 2: session recording and replay (2026-11-10)
Research compared Michiel Ronsse, Koen De Bosschere and Jacques Chassin de Kergommeaux, Execution replay and debugging (2000), https://arxiv.org/abs/cs/0011006 ; Dominik Aumayr, Stefan Marr, Clement Bera, Elisa Gonzalez Boix and Hanspeter Moessenboeck, Efficient and Deterministic Record & Replay for Actor Languages (2018), https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.06267 ; and Nicolas Williams, JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) Text Sequences (RFC 7464, 2015), https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7464.html . Combine ordered message observation at the server's existing write boundary with recipient ids and authoritative ticks. The custom MVR1 binary container preserves bytes without JSON/base64 expansion; an explicit footer rejects interrupted files rather than RFC 7464's optional prefix recovery. It is network-stream playback for spectating and reproduction, not deterministic server-thread or input simulation replay. Existing client codecs reconstruct the world. A bounded asynchronous sink fails visibly rather than dropping messages. Node Buffer subviews are copied into independent Uint8Arrays. No foreign source, companion code, demo, external asset or timing result.

Compared Alan Baker, Mehmet Oguz Derin and David Neto (editors), *WebGPU Shading Language* (W3C, 2026), https://www.w3.org/TR/WGSL/ , with the GPU for the Web Working Group, *WebGPU* (2026), https://www.w3.org/TR/webgpu/ , and Jos Stam, *Stable Fluids* (SIGGRAPH 1999), https://graphics.stanford.edu/courses/cs448-01-spring/papers/stam.pdf . ## Batch 270 job 2: VFX lifetime dynamics
Compared William T. Reeves, Particle Systems: A Technique for Modeling a Class of Fuzzy Objects (1983), https://www.evl.uic.edu/aej/527/papers/Reeves1983.pdf (lifetime property evolution), and Andrew Witkin, Particle System Dynamics (1997), https://www.cs.cmu.edu/afs/cs/user/baraff/www/sigcourse/notesc.pdf (state integration). ## Batch 193 job 1: optional HueGrade (2026-11-10)
Compared Alvy Ray Smith, Color Gamut Transform Pairs (SIGGRAPH 1978), https://alvyray.com/Papers/CG/color78.pdf ; Tab Atkins Jr., Chris Lilley and Lea Verou (editors), CSS Color Module Level 4 (W3C 2026), https://www.w3.org/TR/css-color-4/#hue-interpolation ; and the pmndrs HueSaturationEffect public API, https://pmndrs.github.io/postprocessing/public/docs/class/src/effects/HueSaturationEffect.js~HueSaturationEffect.html (accessed 2026-11-10). Smith's nontrigonometric HSV coordinates retain extrema under rotation; W3C motivates circular hue and powerless achromatic hue. Unlike shortest-path interpolation of absolute target angles, offsets are authored signed degrees and interpolated directly across the periodic input seam. Public rival docs establish global hue and saturation controls; HueGrade combines that behaviour with existing Grade wheels, curves and hue saturation and adds selective hue-against-hue points. This is behaviour parity, not a claim of identical rival pixels: HSV rotation is not a luma-axis rotation. No rival source or companion code was read. Native and compatibility GPU swatches test primary cycles, signed rotation, the periodic seam and neutral colours.

Research combined Jacob Ziv and Abraham Lempel, A Universal Algorithm for Sequential Data Compression (1977, https://doi.org/10.1109/TIT.1977.1055714), for bounded history and overlapping matches; Yann Collet and Murray Kucherawy, Zstandard Compression and the application/zstd Media Type, RFC 8878 (2021, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8878.html), for frames, checksums and limits; Yann Collet, LZ4 Frame Format Description v1.6.5 (2026, https://github.com/lz4/lz4/blob/dev/doc/lz4_Frame_format.md) and LZ4 Block Format Description (2026, https://github.com/lz4/lz4/blob/dev/doc/lz4_Block_format.md), for independent/linked blocks, dictionaries and concatenation; and Yann Collet, xxHash fast digest algorithm v0.2.0 (2023, https://github.com/Cyan4973/xxHash/blob/release/doc/xxhash_spec.md), for descriptor/block/content checks. ## Batch 173 job 3: cinematic volume transport (2026-11-10)
Research compared the finite local spherical integral, directional occlusion and the full radiative-transfer estimator before implementation. No companion code or other engine source was read.
- Frida Hernell, Patric Ljung and Anders Ynnerman, *Local Ambient Occlusion in Direct Volume Rendering* (2010), IEEE TVCG 16:548-559, https://doi.org/10.1109/TVCG.2009.45, paper https://www.diva-portal.org/smash/get/diva2:321233/FULLTEXT01.pdf. Integrate transmittance over finite-radius sphere directions, rather than gradient-only darkening. Our Fibonacci angular quadrature evaluates the classified extinction directly, avoiding an expensive precomputed volume after classifier edits.
- Mathias Schott, Vincent Pegoraro, Charles Hansen, Kevin Boulanger and Kadi Bouatouch, *A Directional Occlusion Shading Model for Interactive Direct Volume Rendering* (2009), https://diglib.eg.org/items/90433cc3-3b04-42eb-b2ba-a959c15c08e6, paper https://cgl.ethz.ch/teaching/scivis_common/Literature/Schott2009.pdf. Use directional radiative attenuation, with Beer-Lambert integration toward a distant light. We evaluate rays, rather than reproduce its slice-propagated cone implementation; the directional-light limit has an independent homogeneous-slab solution.
- Thomas Kroes, Frits H. Post and Charl P. Botha, *Exposure Render: An Interactive Photo-Realistic Volume Rendering Framework* (2012), PLOS ONE 7:e38586, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3388083/. Combine stochastic optical-depth collisions, next-event directional lighting, sampled scattering paths and progressive linear-radiance accumulation. Piecewise-constant per-segment extinction inverts cumulative optical depth directly, without a guessed density majorant or null-collision bias. Russian roulette preserves energy after the third event.
- Louis G. Henyey and Jesse L. Greenstein, *Diffuse radiation in the Galaxy* (1941), Astrophysical Journal 93:70, https://doi.org/10.1086/144246; NIST phase-function definition https://pages.nist.gov/SCATMECH/docs/phase.htm. Derive the normalized HG phase and inverse CDF; use its isotropic limit near g=0. Positive g samples forward along propagation. The direct-light estimator uses p normalised over the sphere, as Pharr, Jakob and Humphreys, *Physically Based Rendering*, 4th ed. (2023), section 11.3, https://pbr-book.org/4ed/Volume_Scattering/Phase_Functions (read 2026-11-15), defines it (isotropic 1/(4 pi)); the single-scatter march uses the same isotropic 1/(4 pi), so both paths treat `light` as the irradiance of the distant light (default 8.8, the old 0.7 times 4 pi, so the default image is unchanged). Until 2026-11-15 the estimator used 4*pi*p and the march an implicit phase of 1. Environment escape uses the sampled phase PDF cancellation.
- Kitware, *Cinematic Volume Rendering in Your Web Browser* (2022), https://www.kitware.com/cinematic-volume-rendering/, and *vtk.js VolumeMapper API*, https://kitware.github.io/vtk-js/api/Rendering_Core_VolumeMapper.html (accessed 2026-11-10). Compared public behaviour: independently enabled local occlusion and volumetric shadows, volume opacity participating in light attenuation. Margo additionally exposes progressive multiple scattering, camera-rest reset and exact work counters. This is a comparison of the requested lighting row, not a full vtk.js feature claim or measured rival timing.
- EMDB, *Map format*, https://files.wwpdb.org/pub/emdb/doc/Map-format/current/EMDB_map_format.pdf; PDBe public-data statement https://www.ebi.ac.uk/pdbe/about/public-data-access-statement. The offline EMD-8117 reducer reads orthogonal XYZ mode-2 maps from the specification, retains stride-3 original samples and records source/output hashes. No general MRC API is claimed. Dataset CC0 and the reused TCIA CC BY 3.0 data stay separately attributed in the demo and source records.

Buss, Introduction to Inverse Kinematics with Jacobian Transpose, Pseudoinverse and Damped Least Squares methods (2009), https://people.csail.mit.edu/jbarry/spring2011PR2/readings/jactrans.pdf ; Kevin M. Lynch and Frank C. ## Batch 271 job 4: anisotropic Kuwahara
Compared Jan Eric Kyprianidis, Henry Kang and Jurgen Dollner, *Image and Video Abstraction by Anisotropic Kuwahara Filtering* (2009), https://www.kyprianidis.com/p/pg2009/jkyprian-pg2009.pdf ; Jan Eric Kyprianidis, Amir Semmo, Henry Kang and Jurgen Dollner, *Anisotropic Kuwahara Filtering with Polynomial Weighting Functions* (2010), https://www.kyprianidis.com/p/tpcg2010/jkyprian-tpcg2010.pdf ; and Holger Wendland, *Piecewise polynomial, positive definite and compactly supported radial functions of minimal degree* (1995), https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02123482 . RGB Sobel tensors are smoothed by a separable five-tap binomial Gaussian approximation; the minor eigenvector orients an area-preserving ellipse with eight overlapping polynomial sectors. Sector means combine by summed RGB variance. A Wendland C2 radial envelope (1-r)^4(1+4r) multiplies the Gaussian: weights reach zero smoothly at the unit ellipse, preventing FP32 membership changes from injecting finite perimeter samples. The original hard cutoff failed the circular GPU oracle by three colour codes; the unchanged one-code bar passes after this support fix. No paper companion code or rival implementation was read. W3C WebGPU/WGSL (2026), https://www.w3.org/TR/webgpu/ and https://www.w3.org/TR/WGSL/ , define explicit unfilterable-float tensor bindings and retained per-view resources. Original analytic image fixtures only; no demo asset or speed claim. Batch 132 audit correction (lane I, 2026-11-10): the sector polynomial used eta = 2 (zeta + cos(pi/4)), the eta of a zero-crossing meeting the unit circle at gamma = pi/4, which is the paper's upper bound 2 pi / N for N = 8, and the CPU reference copied it. Both now use the paper's choice gamma = 3 pi / (2N) = 3 pi / 16, eta = (zeta + cos gamma) / sin^2 gamma (3.77 at zeta = 1/3, the value the paper prints); zeta = 2 / r is unchanged. The GPU oracle is unchanged and passes with worst error 0 native and MARGO_COMPAT=1.

## Batch 274 dense decompositions

Clean-room implementation combines partial-pivoted LU for solve/inverse/determinants, lower Cholesky, Householder QR, one-sided cyclic Jacobi SVD, and symmetric Jacobi eigenpairs. SVD never forms A^T A. Wide matrices transpose and swap factors; rank-zero and full orthogonal factors use twice-reorthogonalized canonical basis completion. Scaled norms avoid unnecessary overflow. No companion code or rival source was read.

Sources: James Demmel and Kresimir Veselic, "Jacobi's Method is More Accurate than QR" (1992), https://doi.org/10.1137/0613074 (relative stopping and one-sided rotations); Gene H. Golub and Christian Reinsch, "Singular Value Decomposition and Least Squares Solutions" (1970), https://people.duke.edu/~hpgavin/SystemID/References/Golub%2BReinsch-NM-1970.pdf (factor conventions, direct decomposition versus squared conditioning; algorithm source listings were not used); Nicholas J. Higham, "Accuracy and Stability of Numerical Algorithms", second edition (2002), chapters 9, 10 and 19, https://doi.org/10.1137/1.9780898718027 (pivoted elimination, positive-definite factorization and Householder stability). Rotations were chosen over bidiagonal QR for a compact common symmetric/SVD implementation; Householder QR remains independent of the Jacobi iteration.

Batch 274 capture lifecycle repair uses resource ownership retirement from Ecma International, ECMAScript specification DisposeResources (2026 draft), https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-disposeresources, alongside the Node.js contributors, Child process event close/exit documentation (2026), https://nodejs.org/api/child_process.html#event-close. The caller's successful early close must relinquish the final-cleanup owner; awaiting a second acknowledgement from a released host is invalid. Only scripts/basic-scene-network.mjs changes; the host/transport/shutdown implementations stay unchanged.

Empty reduced factors follow the shape algebra in the Consortium for Python Data API Standards, QR specification (2025.12), https://data-apis.org/array-api/latest/extensions/generated/array_api.linalg.qr.html. Zero-size result buffers need no matrix factorization; the work-counter regression proves 64 to zero kernel calls with identical empty factor shapes. This avoids work proportional to a virtual batch dimension without changing numerical work for nonempty results.

## Batch 173 job 4: volume sampling and scene depth (2026-11-10)
Research compared conservative range skipping, adaptive integration, precise intersection refinement and spatial/temporal noise before building. No other engine files, source or companion code were used.
- Jens Kruger and Rudiger Westermann, *Acceleration Techniques for GPU-based Volume Rendering* (2003), IEEE Visualization, https://doi.org/10.1109/VISUAL.2003.1250384, https://www.cs.cit.tum.de/fileadmin/w00cfj/cg/Research/Publications/2003/Acceleration_Techniques_for_GPU-based_Volume_Rendering/vis03-rc.pdf. Use conservative scalar intervals to avoid work only where classification is transparent. Our GPU-generated block ranges include interpolation halos; a classifier envelope includes every gradient row and the full support between adjacent LUT entries, not merely their endpoints.
- Christian Sigg, *Representation and Rendering of Implicit Surfaces* (2006), ETH thesis, chapter 6 sections 6.2 and 6.3, https://cgl.ethz.ch/Downloads/Publications/Dissertations/Sig06.pdf. Compare block walking and variation-dependent sampling, then refine the first detected sign-changing interval by bisection. Only chapter 6 prose/math was used, not the shader appendix. Our refined lookup explicitly interpolates eight voxel corners in float32, so hardware texture-filter subtexel quantization cannot defeat a finer bisection.
- Robert Ulichney, *The void-and-cluster method for dither array generation* (1993), https://cv.ulichney.com/papers/1993-void-cluster.pdf; *Filter Design for Void-and-Cluster Dither Arrays* (1994), https://cv.ulichney.com/papers/1994-filter-design.pdf. Build a periodic Gaussian-density relaxation and full rank permutation offline, sigma 1.5, rather than copy a mask. scripts/prepare-sciviz-blue-noise.py produces the 32x32 scalar rank tile; no costly CPU loop runs in the browser.
- Alan Wolfe, Nathan Morrical, Tomas Akenine-Moller and Ravi Ramamoorthi, *Scalar Spatiotemporal Blue Noise Masks* (2021 preprint, EGSR 2022), https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.09629, https://arxiv.org/html/2112.09629v1. Compare spatial versus temporal error. The quality entry uses a static spatial blue-noise tile; it does not claim the paper's spatiotemporal spectrum. The permutation and low-frequency suppression are checked independently in volume-quality.test.js.
- W3C GPU for the Web Working Group, *WebGPU* (2026 Candidate Recommendation), https://www.w3.org/TR/webgpu/#plain-color-formats and https://www.w3.org/TR/webgpu/#render-pass-encoder. Respect sampled/write attachment alias rules: snapshot opaque depth before transparent integration. Resolve reversed-Z multisamples by their maximum, reconstruct the actual world-space hit using inverse projection, then transform it into each ray's metric. Keep progressive colour as float32; pack exact work counters into RG32uint so colour, per-pixel depth/count history and counters fit the baseline 32-byte attachment budget.
- Kitware, *vtk.js VolumeMapper API*, https://kitware.github.io/vtk-js/api/Rendering_Core_VolumeMapper.html (public contract reviewed 2026-11-10). Compare sample-distance controls, jitter and opaque-depth mixing; Margo's requested row additionally provides independent min/max skipping, adaptive segment lengths and first-hit bisection. This is feature-row coverage, not a timing comparison or full-library parity claim.

# Batch 177 job 1: optional 2D contour plots

New `/contour2d` is independent of the mesh `/contour` entry and the root. No rival implementation or companion code was read. Research compared bilinear marching squares with triangulated linear interpolation and combined the following public descriptions:

- G. M. Nielson and B. Hamann, 1991, *The Asymptotic Decider: Resolving the Ambiguity in Marching Cubes*, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1109/VISUAL.1991.175782). A square's saddle uses the sign of `(v0-t)(v2-t)-(v1-t)(v3-t)`, with a documented 0-2 tie. Each band is the even-odd difference of adjacent superlevel polygon rings, so holes and saddle connectivity agree with isolines.
- A. Bowyer, 1981, *Computing Dirichlet Tessellations*, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1093/comjnl/24.2.162), and D. F. Watson, 1981, *Computing the n-dimensional Delaunay tessellation with application to Voronoi polytopes*, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1093/comjnl/24.2.167). Incremental circumcircle cavities construct the scattered interpolation; all coordinates and values remain caller data.
- C. L. Lawson, 1977, *Software for C1 Surface Interpolation*, [NASA record](https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19770025881). Convex hull fan legalization supplies the initial triangulation, avoiding finite supertriangle errors on thin domains.
- J. R. Shewchuk, 1997, *Adaptive Precision Floating-Point Arithmetic and Fast Robust Geometric Predicates*, [paper](https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~jrs/papers/robustr.pdf). We use conservative floating determinant filters followed by our own exact BigInt dyadic determinant, rather than copying expansion code. Cocircular ties use insertion order.
- W3C SVG Working Group, 2018, *Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) 2*, [painting](https://www.w3.org/TR/SVG2/painting.html) and [text](https://www.w3.org/TR/SVG2/text.html). Even-odd polygon filling, paths and rotated halo labels remain vectors with escaped attributes and title text.

The published [Plotly contour reference](https://plotly.com/javascript/reference/contour/) supplies the black-box behaviour checklist: rectilinear x/y, explicit levels, missing values, fills, isolines and labels. Added beyond that trace: scattered Delaunay input and owned polygon coordinates. Tests independently prove all 16 cell cases, both saddle sides, band area, thin triangulation coverage and empty circumcircles, rather than deriving expected output from a rival. No speed claim or Rust/Wasm gain is asserted; the speed phase retains timing work.

Real demo data are reduced NOAA OISST (US public domain) and ECMWF ERA5 via WeatherBench 2 (Copernicus terms and CC BY 4.0 attribution). Exact sources, reductions, units and SHA-256 are beside the frozen JSON, with a reproducible preparation script. The scattered demo intentionally interpolates across missing sites inside the convex hull; the grid demo masks all incident missing cells.


## Batch 188: Fresnel and contact-preserving reflector blur

Research: Christophe Schlick, *An Inexpensive BRDF Model for Physically-Based Rendering* (1994), https://doi.org/10.1111/1467-8659.1330233 ; Eric Lengyel, *Oblique View Frustum Depth Projection and Clipping* (2005), https://terathon.org/lengyel/Lengyel-Oblique.pdf ; Lance Williams, *Pyramidal Parametrics* (1983), https://doi.org/10.1145/800059.801126 . The combination uses Schlick's angular reflectance and IOR-derived dielectric F0, reconstructs world positions with the inverse oblique capture projection, and selects the existing mip hierarchy by captured geometry's world distance from the plane. This avoids using ordinary perspective linearization on oblique depth, and preserves sharp contact reflections. Public rival documentation compared: https://drei.docs.pmnd.rs/shaders/mesh-reflector-material describes depth-controlled blur and roughness. No rival or companion source read or copied.

The optional PBRReflector subclasses the existing Reflector through protected shader/uniform/depth hooks in PlanarSurface; capture, clipping, normal distortion, layers and restore stay in one implementation. Sampled depth uses aspect depth-only, including depth-stencil capture targets, covered by a CPU regression and the real stencil-capable engine capture. Base color is an artist-selected linear floor term mixed with the Fresnel-weighted reflection; this is not a complete direct-light material or a microfacet ray-traced reflection.

Landing blocker repaired: main commit 72642362b retained two VFX test:gpu members without a separating comma. Removed the obsolete shorter member and retained the complete --all plus --all --compat gate. Regression packages/vfx/test/manifest.test.js parses the manifest and requires one complete GPU gate. Standards researched: Tim Bray (editor), *RFC 8259: The JavaScript Object Notation Data Interchange Format* (2017), https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8259.html section 4; Ecma International, *ECMA-404*, second edition (2017), https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-404.pdf . Both require member separators; RFC 8259 also recommends unique names.

- Jarek Rossignac, *Edgebreaker: Connectivity compression for triangle meshes* (1999), https://faculty.cc.gatech.edu/~jarek/papers/EdgeBreaker.pdf . Abstract read, not the full paper. General entropy rationale only; every serialized ANS equation is independently inverted from the Draco specification.
- Zina H. Cigolle, Sam Donow, Daniel Evangelakos, Michael Mara, Morgan McGuire and Quirin Meyer, *A Survey of Efficient Representations for Independent Unit Vectors* (2014), https://jcgt.org/published/0003/02/01/ . The original normal quantizer evaluates a surrounding 4x4 octahedral lattice using float32 reconstruction from the Draco specification, then canonicalizes equivalent boundary coordinates.

No encoder/decoder implementation source, disassembly, companion code or remembered codec internals was used. The unchanged prebuilt encoder and decoder ran opaquely from the lane's own outside oracle folder. A thrown upstream abort printed one wrapper stack line during the rejected 30-bit normal experiment; it was not consulted for any encoding rule. That upstream abort is not reproduced in a correctness gate. The new encoder's supported syntax is checked independently through the existing Margo native decoder and the prebuilt decoder's public APIs.

The combination preserves every oriented triangle, including degenerate/nonmanifold inputs by splitting disconnected fans, and shares position/attribute seam graphs without merging unequal corner data. Portable predictions include difference, parallelogram, constrained multi-parallelogram, portable UV and geometric normals, with wrap/canonical normal transforms. Raw floats remain exact. The full UINT32 domain uses prediction NONE when its signed wrap range cannot be represented, preventing the old decoder's range rejection while retaining every bit. Regression: packages/exporters/tests/draco-native.test.js.

The original seed search keeps the complete baseline payload as a candidate. Below speed 8 it explores at most eight seeds and at most 8,192 candidate input cells, counted as (index corners + source attribute scalar cells) times candidate count. This bounds candidate input volume, not all internal work. No timing claim follows from it. Speed 10 uses sequential connectivity and builds no topology. All speeds preserve the same quantized values and triangles.

Real Box, Fox, MetalRoughSpheres, CommercialRefrigerator, Lantern and RiggedFigure inputs are existing openly licensed Khronos fixtures with provenance already recorded in the asset notices. Public feature tests exercise the packet ABI, both decoders, exact integer boundaries, shared seams, cancellation, bounded repeated allocation and 3,000 fixed normal directions at six bit depths. The independent replay tests cover handles, holes, disconnected meshes, valence contexts and 256 deterministic arbitrary triangle soups. Byte/error comparisons and the deferred timing obligation are scoped in limits.md and the speed work lists. No core, stage or rendering-backend source changes.

Batch 136 replacement proof extends the same specification-derived implementation with prediction-degree attribute traversal, bounded RAW rANS alphabets below 2^20, and circular distance for modular normal residuals. A residual of modulus minus one represents minus one; treating it as a large unsigned error needlessly changes geometric-normal signs and increases the flip stream. Both sign policies remain complete payload candidates, including probability tables and flip bits. The smaller actual payload wins, since circular distance alone need not minimize entropy. The alternate traversal retains the depth-first payload and changes only the base vertex group; corner seam groups retain their published depth-first descriptor. Histogram, probability and ordering storage are bounded to 16 MiB at the RAW alphabet cap in wasm32. Sparse wider alphabets use tagged symbols.

## Batch 274 job 4: missing neural-network layers

Research compared and combined, with no rival or companion implementation code used:
- Sergey Ioffe and Christian Szegedy, *Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift* (2015), https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.03167 . Batch-statistic training and saved inference statistics are distinct, with explicit affine parameters.
- Yuxin Wu and Kaiming He, *Group Normalization* (2018), https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.08494 . Normalize within sample/channel groups; no batch running state.
- Sepp Hochreiter and Jurgen Schmidhuber, *Long Short-Term Memory* (1997), https://doi.org/10.1162/neco.1997.9.8.1735 . Explicit cell and hidden state preserve the additive memory path.
- Kyunghyun Cho, Bart van Merrienboer, Caglar Gulcehre, Dzmitry Bahdanau, Fethi Bougares, Holger Schwenk and Yoshua Bengio, *Learning Phrase Representations using RNN Encoder-Decoder for Statistical Machine Translation* (2014), https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.1078 . Separate reset, update and candidate gates.
- ONNX contributors, *ConvTranspose*, *Resize*, *LSTM* and *GRU operator specifications* (2026), https://onnx.ai/onnx/operators/onnx__ConvTranspose.html , https://onnx.ai/onnx/operators/onnx__Resize.html , https://onnx.ai/onnx/operators/onnx__LSTM.html , https://onnx.ai/onnx/operators/onnx__GRU.html . These give spatial geometry, pixel-center coordinates and recurrent state/sequence conventions. No linked sample operator code was used.
- TensorFlow.js contributors, *Layers API* (public descriptions only), https://js.tensorflow.org/api/latest/ . The requested row checklist is train/eval normalization, transposed convolution, differentiable LSTM/GRU with explicit states, and upsampling. Extra coverage includes grouped/dilated transpose, stacked/bidirectional recurrent sequences, padded lengths, three spatial ranks and bicubic interpolation. Defaults/conventions below are explicit; no identical serialized-weight layout claim is made.

All arithmetic composes Margo's existing Tensor tape and compute primitives. Transposed convolution gathers each output's valid input taps and multiplies by grouped weights; the independent test reference scatters each input into output positions. An explicit where mask prevents padding from turning an unrelated NaN into a contribution. Interpolation gathers clamped neighbors with nearest, half-pixel linear or cubic-convolution weights (a=-0.75). Its backward pass sums repeated readers through scatter. New index/weight tables are CPU-authored metadata, not a new numerical execution backend; no speed claim is made.

BatchNorm uses biased variance for normalization and unbiased variance in running buffers, with momentum as the NEW batch contribution, default 0.1. LSTM gate layout is i,f,g,o. GRU layout is r,z,n and resets the projected recurrent candidate, including its bias. Recurrent output time order is retained for both directions. Module state persistence now delegates to child state dictionaries, so a nested BatchNorm's running statistics and batch count are restored, while each parameter is read/written once. The regression is the nested Sequential case in nn-extra-cases.js.

Evidence: 38 shared analytic/gradient/state cases on JavaScript CPU, SIMD CPU, WebGPU and compatibility; independent finite differences for every input of norms, transpose and stacked/bidirectional LSTM/GRU; exact gradient counts for overlap and interpolation; and a live-buffer counter proving forward/backward temporary disposal. No new external data or demo was introduced.

The signature now requires the squared-cosine factor, including renamed variables and pow(cosine,2). Positive regressions retain real GGX copies; negative regressions cover both transpose axes and cubic interpolation. Sources compared: Chanchal K. Roy and James R. Cordy, A Survey on Software Clone Detection Research (2007), https://clones.usask.ca/cdl/ ; Chanchal K. Roy, James R. Cordy and Rainer Koschke, Comparison and Evaluation of Code Clone Detection Techniques and Tools: A Qualitative Approach (2009), https://research.cs.queensu.ca/home/cordy/Papers/RCK_SCP_Clones.pdf ; Bruce Walter, Stephen R. Marschner, Hongsong Li and Kenneth E. Torrance, Microfacet Models for Refraction through Rough Surfaces (2007), https://www.cs.cornell.edu/~srm/publications/EGSR07-btdf.pdf . ## Review 4: finite Wang weights (2026-11-10)

Compared Thorbjorn Lindeijer and Tiled contributors, JSON Map Format, tile probability and Wang metadata (2026), https://doc.mapeditor.org/en/stable/reference/json-map-format/ ; and Matt Pharr, Wenzel Jakob and Greg Humphreys, Physically Based Rendering: From Theory to Implementation, fourth edition, section 2.3 Sampling Using the Inversion Method (2023), https://www.pbr-book.org/4ed/Monte_Carlo_Integration/Sampling_Using_the_Inversion_Method . The probability is a relative weight, w_i / sum(w), so dividing all positive candidates by their largest weight preserves the distribution and bounds the sum by the candidate count. This avoids Infinity for weights [1e308,1e308] and avoids rounding an entire subnormal interval away. The last positive candidate owns any rounded upper endpoint. The regression fails before the fix and compares 512 seeded cells against the same normalized weights, including unequal ratios, zero exclusions and all-zero/no-match results. Implemented from these mathematical descriptions; no external implementation was copied or adapted.

## Batch 173 job 6: tetrahedral direct volume rendering (2026-11-10)
Compared projected tetrahedra, adjacency ray casting, half-space traversal and spatial entry queries before writing the implementation. No engine source, companion source or external implementation files were used.
- Michael P. Garrity, *Raytracing irregular volume data* (1990), https://doi.org/10.1145/99307.99316 . Adjacency ray casting is the requested method; the traversal details were also cross-checked against the later open report below.
- Peter Shirley and Allan Tuchman, *A Polygonal Approximation to Direct Scalar Volume Rendering* (1990), https://cgl.ethz.ch/teaching/scivis_common/Literature/ShirleyTuchman90.pdf . Compare linear finite-element reconstruction, physical ray integration and the visibility-order requirements of projected cells. Choose direct rays instead of global per-view sorting.
- Ares Lagae and Philip Dutre, *Accelerating Ray Tracing using Constrained Tetrahedralizations* (2008), report CW 513, section 4, https://graphics.cs.kuleuven.be/publications/LD08ARTCTb/LD08ARTCTb_paper.pdf . Use four barycentric half-spaces to obtain an exact convex-cell ray interval and its opposite-vertex neighbour. A stackless cell-bounds tree handles initial entry, holes, disconnected components and edge/vertex crossings with no positive-length adjacent interval. No geometric epsilon advances are used to jump over thin cells.
- Ingo Wald, Heiko Friedrich, Aaron Knoll and Charles D. Hansen, *Interactive Isosurface Ray Tracing of Time-Varying Tetrahedral Volumes* (2007), https://www.sci.utah.edu/~wald/Publications/2007/TettyTR/download/tettyTR.pdf . Compare tetrahedral finite-element reconstruction and a cell BVH. Our ray caster uses a scalar mesh snapshot and a stackless tree; it does not implement the paper's isopolygon or SIMD packet algorithms.
- Nicholas J. Higham, *Accuracy and Stability of Numerical Algorithms*, second edition (2002), vector norms, https://doi.org/10.1137/1.9780898718027 ; Higham, *What Is a Vector Norm?* (2021 archive), https://nhigham.com/2021/ . Compare the overflow/underflow risk of squaring dimensional coordinates with bounded normalized metrics. Normalize the physical extents and reference distance by the same maximum extent before the shader evaluates its norm. This preserves physical extinction at scales 1e-20 and 1e20; it is not a change to the engine coordinate convention.
- Alan Baker, Mehmet Oguz Derin and David Neto (editors), *WebGPU Shading Language* (2026), pow built-in, https://www.w3.org/TR/WGSL/#pow-builtin . Keep exact opaque opacity 1 for positive-length intervals rather than artificially capping the classifier alpha below 1; regression referenceStep=1000 still gives fully opaque red.
- Christopher L. Rumsey, Brian R. Smith and George P. Huang, *Description of a Website Resource for Turbulence Modeling Verification and Validation* (2010), https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20100025022/downloads/20100025022.pdf ; NASA TMR, *SA Expected Results - 2D Zero Pressure Gradient Flat Plate* (2026 access), https://tmbwg.github.io/turbmodels/flatplate_sa.html . The two-dimensional source is not presented as a new three-dimensional simulation.
