- Housen and Holsapple 2011's ejecta form v ~ (x / R)^(-1/mu) and its 45 degree launch, as "Ejecta distribution from
  impact craters on Ryugu" (arXiv:2205.06607, Table B1 and eqs. 1 and 2) reprints it (the 2011 paper was not obtained).
- M. D. Nordyke, "On cratering", UCRL-6578, 1961 (Appendix A and Table III: the alluvium HE shots fitted, and the basalt
  shots, read); M. D. Nordyke and M. M. Williamson, "The Sedan event", PNE-242F, 1965 (sections 2.3, 2.4 and 6.1.2:
  Sedan's crater, its ejecta's spread and spall speed, the nuclear radii's shortfall, read); J. Toman, "Summary of
  nuclear-excavation applications", 1970 (Table IV: Danny Boy, Cabriolet, Schooner, their bulking, read); H. F. Cooper,
  RDA-TR-2604-001, 1976 (section 1.2: a factor of 2 in volume between identical shots, read); T. Waltham, Mercian
  Geologist 15(2), 2001, and G. Fielder and J. E. Guest, Comm. Lunar Planet. Lab. 115, 1968 (Fauld, read).
- T. R. McGetchin, M. Settle and J. W. Head, EPSL 20, 1973: the blanket's r^-3, as Minton et al. (arXiv:1902.07746) quote
  it (not obtained).
No cratering or hydrocode code was read. Fitting the burial curves, the rim's (R / r)^3 profile, the shells' exact volume
on the bed's vertex areas, and the launch speed's calibration to Sedan are this package's own. A research agent gathered
the documents; every value used was checked on its page before it was used.

### FLUID-07 implicit film matrix and independent incline drops

Alexander Oron, Stephen H. Davis and S. George Bankoff (1997), *Long-scale evolution of thin liquid films*, equations 2.30 and 2.36–2.37, give the film pressure terms from curvature and normal gravity. Leonard W. Schwartz and Richard R. Eley (1998), *Simulation of Droplet Motion on Low-Energy and Heterogeneous Surfaces*, describe the precursor and disjoining pressure for finite contacts. Andrea L. Bertozzi and Mary C. Pugh (1996), *The lubrication approximation for thin viscous films: Regularity and long-time behavior of weak solutions*, describe the degenerate fourth-order equation governing small slopes. The native phase applies the same discrete face matrix in independent ranges. The global dot products and convergence decisions use their established order. [Oron, Davis and Bankoff](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.69.931) · [Schwartz and Eley](https://doi.org/10.1006/jcis.1998.5448) · [Bertozzi and Pugh](https://doi.org/10.1002/%28SICI%291097-0312%28199602%2949%3A2%3C85%3A%3AAID-CPA1%3E3.0.CO%3B2-2)

Bert Blocken and Jan Carmeliet (2004), *A review of wind-driven rain research in building science*, describe precipitation flux through the projected area. The directed rolling-window comparison independently sums that projection on the moving plane. The measured sliding-drop diagnostic uses controlled 47V10 volumes, material properties and inclination from Nolwenn Le Grand, Adrian Daerr and Laurent Limat (2005). Coat angles come from independent static observations by Thomas Podgorski (2000). Two velocity markers in Figure 7 are held out. [Wind-driven rain](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jweia.2004.06.003) · [Sliding-drop experiment](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0022112005006105) · [Podgorski thesis (2000)](https://theses.hal.science/tel-00003231) · [Podgorski, Flesselles and Limat (2001)](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.87.036102)

### BREAK-03 native membrane work and independent steel tubes

Juan C. Simo and Robert L. Taylor (1986), *A return mapping algorithm for plane stress elastoplasticity*, give the predictor and plastic correction structure. Rodney Hill (1948), *A theory of the yielding and plastic flow of anisotropic metals*, gives the quadratic anisotropic yield form. Ted Belytschko, Jerry I. Lin and Chen-Shyh Tsay (1984), *Explicit algorithms for the nonlinear dynamics of shells*, describe shell element evaluation in explicit integration. Native workers use those existing constitutive terms in independent face ranges. The caller assembles nodal forces and energy in original face order. [Simo and Taylor](https://doi.org/10.1002/nme.1620220310) · [Hill](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1948.0045) · [Belytschko, Lin and Tsay](https://doi.org/10.1016/0045-7825(84)90026-4)

Young Il Park, Jin-Seong Cho and Jeong-Hwan Kim (2022), *Numerical and Experimental Investigation of Quasi-Static Crushing Behaviors of Steel Tubular Structures*, reproduce Jung's six ASTM A500 tube compression tests. The published specimen geometry and tensile measurements are model inputs. Test forces, terminal strokes and two trace readings are independent outcomes. The numerical comparison applies the existing production reduced model without fitting the measured force. [Park, Cho and Kim](https://doi.org/10.3390/ma15062107)

### SEA-03 native pair evaluation and held-out flume counts

Dalzell (1999), [A note on finite depth second-order wave–wave interactions](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0141118799000085), and Adcock and Draper (2015), [The Second Order Contribution to Wave Crest Amplitude](https://users.ox.ac.uk/~spet1235/2015-TPC-0515%20Adcock.pdf), equations 1–3 and appendix, supply the existing sum and difference convention. SIMD evaluates independent products. The reduction keeps the original scalar sum with the linear contribution added at the start of each component's pair row. To compute the normal, differentiate both factors of each pair and the prescribed spatial window by the product rule. Tromans, Anaturk and Hagemeijer (1991) derive the conditional profile from spectral autocovariance in their design-wave paper. The implementation's compact taper remains an authoring choice.

Dematteis, Grafke, Onorato and Vanden-Eijnden (2019), [Experimental Evidence of Hydrodynamic Instantons](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevX.9.041057), supplied the independent flume observation counts. The script reads the wavemaker spectrum parameters and the separate gauge count from the paper, evaluates the existing second-order model without prescribed crests, and reports the discrepancies. [Reproduction](whitepaper/reproduce.md#sea-03-second-order-waves-and-independent-flume-counts)

### SEA-01 native spatial transport and independent finite-depth comparison

The flux and limiter follow B. P. Leonard (1991), [The ULTIMATE conservative difference scheme applied to unsteady one-dimensional advection](https://doi.org/10.1016/0045-7825(91)90232-U), and the [NOAA WAVEWATCH III 5.16 manual](https://polar.ncep.noaa.gov/waves/wavewatch/manual.v5.16.pdf), §3.3.3, equations 3.12–3.23. Native participants evaluate independent spatial lines and leave the original axis, substep, refraction and source order intact. They do not change the physical law or limiter.

The diagnostic uses the Lake George campaign of I. R. Young and L. A. Verhagen (1996), [The growth of fetch limited waves in water of finite depth, Part 1](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0378-3839(96)00006-3), as tabulated by V. S. Gruijthuijsen (1996), [Validation of the wave prediction model SWAN using field data from Lake George, Australia](https://resolver.tudelft.nl/uuid:a8a1face-a0ef-4307-85cf-7931c92bb6eb), §4.3, figure 4.2 and Appendix I. The ST4 source paper cites a separate later campaign at this lake in its discussion of cumulative breaking. The B/C fetch-growth observations in this comparison were not used to fit coefficients. [Method and controls](whitepaper/reproduce.md#sea-01-accepted-wave-transport-and-lake-george)

## Alpine wildflowers: procedural/forbs (2026-11-28)

Plants round 1 for the Above the Treeline film: the meadow had no forbs. Written clean room from these papers and
floras; no plant generator's code was read.

- Phyllotaxis of the cushion and of the daisy discs: H. Vogel, "A better way to construct the sunflower head",
  Mathematical Biosciences 44, 1979, https://doi.org/10.1016/0025-5564(79)90080-4.
- Rosette, stem and inflorescence structure (racemes, spikes, capitula): P. Prusinkiewicz and A. Lindenmayer, The
  Algorithmic Beauty of Plants, Springer 1990, http://algorithmicbotany.org/papers/#abop.
- Flower shapes from petal profiles and floral diagrams: T. Ijiri, S. Owada, M. Okabe and T. Igarashi, "Floral
  diagrams and inflorescences: interactive flower modeling using botanical structural constraints", ACM SIGGRAPH 2005,
  https://doi.org/10.1145/1073204.1073253.
- Inflorescence architecture and variation: P. Prusinkiewicz, Y. Erasmus, B. Lane, L. D. Harder and E. Coen,
  "Evolution and development of inflorescence architectures", Science 316, 2007, https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1140429.
- Heights, leaf shapes and head counts: Flora of North America (Arnica cordifolia, Gentiana parryi, Erigeron /
  Oreostemma alpigenum, Bistorta bistortoides, Silene acaulis), http://floranorthamerica.org.
- Petal and leaf colour: FReD, the Floral Reflectance Database, S. E. J. Arnold, S. Faruq, V. Savolainen, P. W.
  McOwan and L. Chittka, PLoS ONE 5(12) e14287, 2010, https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0014287 (data only,
  credited in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md), integrated with @margoengine/optics/spectrum.

Combined: Vogel's golden-angle spiral places cushion stars and disc florets; leaves and rays are strips bent along a
profile (ovate, lanceolate, spatulate, strap) as in Ijiri et al.; stems and heads follow the raceme, spike and
capitulum forms of Prusinkiewicz and Lindenmayer. Each part is its own geometry so the instancer can colour it with its
measured spectrum. Scatter gained `reach` as an exact override and inside clearings for this (moss skirts at rock bases).

## IK limbs kept out of the body, and a relaxed hand: animator/ik, rigging/ik (2026-11-28)

Scope: `solveLimbIK`'s `avoid` and `twist`, and `rigging/ik`'s use of the body's volumes and its `hand` option
(KB-RIG-REACHTRUNK1). Written from the sources below; no other engine's or tool's code was read.

- The swivel searched for the nearest value that is both inside the joint ranges and free of collision with the body:
  M. Kallmann, "Analytical inverse kinematics with body posture control", Computer Animation and Virtual Worlds
  19(2):79-91, 2008, https://doi.org/10.1002/cav.176 ; D. Tolani, A. Goswami and N. I. Badler, Graphical Models
  62(5):353-388, 2000, https://doi.org/10.1006/gmod.2000.0528 (one swivel angle per limb).
- The body's volumes: capsules of the ANSUR II mean girths (C. C. Gordon et al., "2012 Anthropometric survey of U.S.
  Army personnel", NATICK/TR-15/007, 2014), the closest points of two segments as in C. Ericson, "Real-Time Collision
  Detection", Morgan Kaufmann 2005, section 5.1.9. The IK keeps them apart past 0.8 of their radii, a little stricter
  than the pose checker's 0.7, so a solved reach passes the checker.
- The relaxed hand: the forearm's zero is the neutral of ISO/IEC 19774-1:2019 (HAnim), clause 4.8.2, palms toward the
  thighs with the arm hanging, the mid-position between pronation and supination (A. I. Kapandji, "The Physiology of the
  Joints", vol. 1, the forearm's position of reference); the hand is left at the fitted body's neutral.

Margo's own: the depth inside the body turned into an angle seen from the shoulder or hip and added to the range
excess the swivel search already minimised, so one search serves both; the relaxed hand set before the solve so the
reach is solved with the hand it ends with.

### SEA-05 native radiation stress and measured barred surf

Longuet-Higgins and Stewart (1964), [Radiation stresses in water waves](https://doi.org/10.1016/0011-7471(64)90001-4), §1 and §7, derive the progressive-wave tensor and its rotation. Roelvink et al. (2009), [Modelling storm impacts on beaches, dunes and barrier islands](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.coastaleng.2009.08.006), §3.2, give the directional and roller stresses and the force from their negative divergence. Native workers compute equal per-cell directional sums, the existing roller stresses and Stokes terms, then apply centered differences once all moments are available. The reduction retains the original bin order.

Boers (1996), [Simulation of a surf zone with a barred beach](https://resolver.tudelft.nl/uuid:22dfbc0a-adf8-44cb-9659-9d0a366c88d6), measured the flume conditions. Moghimi et al. (2020), [Development of an ESMF Based Flexible Coupling Application of ADCIRC and WAVEWATCH III for High Fidelity Coastal Inundation Studies](https://doi.org/10.3390/jmse8050308), Table 3 and figure 10, report the offshore forcing and independently measured wave-height and mean-level markers. Daly et al. (2012), [Validation of an advective-deterministic approach to short wave breaking in a surf-beat model](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.coastaleng.2011.08.001), figure 2, provide physical bed coordinates. Janssen, Battjes and van Dongeren (2003), [Long waves induced by short-wave groups over a sloping bottom](https://doi.org/10.1029/2002JC001515), §2.1 and Table 1, give experiment metadata and gauge placement. No competing model's fitted coefficients were used. [Reproduction](whitepaper/reproduce.md#sea-05-accepted-surf-and-boers-flume-gauges)

## Rock facets filtered by footprint, fog past the scene's end: terrain rock, sky fog (2026-11-28)

Above the Treeline look round 5: jointed rock blocks 200 to 600 m away read as low-poly shards (each Voronoi cell a flat
tilted plane with a hard switch at its edge and dark joint lines), and where the world ended before the horizon the sky's
own horizon colour showed as a flat band under the far ranges. Sources read (papers only, no companion code):

- M. Toksvig, "Mipmapping normal maps", Journal of Graphics Tools 10(3), 2005,
  https://doi.org/10.1080/2151237X.2005.10129203 (normal detail finer than a pixel is averaged away, not sampled).
- E. Bruneton and F. Neyret, "A survey of nonlinear prefiltering methods for efficient and accurate surface shading",
  IEEE TVCG 18(2), 2012, https://doi.org/10.1109/TVCG.2011.81 (fading meso-scale normal variation with the footprint so
  the mean shading holds; the relief, tone and joint shade fall with the block's size in pixels).
- S. Worley, "A cellular texture basis function", SIGGRAPH 1996, https://doi.org/10.1145/237170.237267 (F2 - F1 as the
  distance to a cell edge: the tilt and tone blend into the second-nearest cell across it, so the normal is continuous).
- E. Bruneton and F. Neyret, "Precomputed atmospheric scattering", EGSR 2008, https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-8659.2008.01245.x
  (aerial perspective: the in-scattered light along a ray tends to its limit as the ray's optical depth grows, so a ray
  below the horizon that meets nothing in the scene takes the fog's colour at infinity, not the sky's horizon).

Above the Treeline look round 5: bistort spikes of solid florets on a golden-angle lattice read as pine cones, arnica as
flat yellow discs, moss campion cushions as lily pads, and the flowers vanished past the middle ring. Sources read:

  botanical structural constraints", SIGGRAPH 2005, https://doi.org/10.1145/1073204.1073253 (heads as an axis with

  https://doi.org/10.1145/1276377.1276476 (a simplified far plant keeps the area and colour its detail covered).

Margo's own: the Rodrigues turn of a head built upright onto its nodding axis; a cushion's rosettes as a product of

### SEA-07 native Sun, Moon and atmospheric potential

Pugh and Woodworth (2014), [Sea-Level Science](https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9781139235778), Chapter 3, and Stewart, [Introduction to Physical Oceanography](https://geo.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Oceanography/Introduction_to_Physical_Oceanography_%28Stewart%29/17%3A_Coastal_Processes_and_Tides/17.4%3A_Theory_of_Ocean_Tides), §17.4, give the tide-generating potential with constant and uniform-acceleration terms removed. Native cells evaluate the existing rationalized Newton expression for the Sun and Moon using the published Earth-fixed vectors. The wet pressure and tide sums use the original row order. The next phase forms the same pressure head and relative equilibrium tide. Luettich and Westerink (2004), [Formulation and numerical implementation of ADCIRC](https://adcirc.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/2255/2013/07/adcirc_theory_2004_12_08.pdf), Eq. 1.13, gives the separate atmospheric and equilibrium-potential gradients in depth-integrated momentum.

### WebGL2 layer: warm frames held for their links, replayed in slices, framebuffer status per signature (KB-QUALITY-WARMSERIAL1, KB-COMPAT-FBSTATUS1)

Jie Chen, Geoff Lang and the Khronos WebGL Working Group, *KHR_parallel_shader_compile* (WebGL extension 37,
revision 6, 2020), https://registry.khronos.org/webgl/extensions/KHR_parallel_shader_compile/ : `COMPLETION_STATUS_KHR`
answers without blocking, so compile and link every program first and poll; it reads true on a lost context. Mozilla
contributors, *WebGL best practices* (MDN), https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/WebGL_API/WebGL_best_practices :
`checkFramebufferStatus`, `getBufferSubData`, `getError` and the status gets each force a round trip to the GPU process;
a fence polled with `clientWaitSync(sync, flags, 0)` from a later task waits without blocking. Khronos, *OpenGL ES
Version 3.0.6* (2019), section 4.4.4, https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/specs/es/3.0/es_spec_3.0.pdf : attachment and
whole framebuffer completeness follow from each attached image's object type, internal format, renderbuffer samples,
non-zero size and (for a mutable texture) level, never from which object it is; FRAMEBUFFER_UNSUPPORTED follows from
the combination of formats. Khronos, *WebGL 2.0 Specification*, https://registry.khronos.org/webgl/specs/latest/2.0/ ,
"checkFramebufferStatus may return FRAMEBUFFER_INCOMPLETE_DIMENSIONS" (equal widths and heights) and "Framebuffer color
attachments" (one image at one colour point). Derived here: the queue's link hold, its replay in tasks of about 50 ms
resumed between commands outside a render pass with a fence between tasks, and the status cache keyed by kind, format,
size and point. Search results naming Firefox, WebKit and public_webgl threads were not opened and are not cited. No
browser, ANGLE or other engine source was read.

### ATMO-04 size-dependent sedimentation and native rain trajectories

Kaitlyn Loftus and Robin Wordsworth (2021), [The Physics of Falling Raindrops in Diverse Planetary Atmospheres](https://doi.org/10.1029/2020JE006653), equations 8 and 9, give the size-dependent terminal balance and the sum of the air's vertical motion and a drop's settling velocity. Daniel Dawson II, Edward Mansell, Youngsun Jung, Ming Xue, Asher Schenkman and Alexander Ryzhkov (2015), [Does Wind Shear Cause Hydrometeor Size Sorting?](https://doi.org/10.1175/JAS-D-14-0084.1), describe the downwind displacement as a function of terminal velocity, layer depth and mean storm-relative wind. John Lane et al. (2009), [Spatial and Temporal Extrapolation of Disdrometer Size Distributions Based on a Lagrangian Trajectory Model of Falling Rain](https://arxiv.org/abs/0906.1614), compare advection with delayed size-specific arrival. The field uses descending midpoint characteristics and flux weights proportional to particle mass, settling speed and its reference concentration.

Fabrice Veron and Luc Mieussens (2016), [A Kinetic Model for Particle–Surface Interaction Applied to Rain Falling on Water Waves](https://doi.org/10.1017/jfm.2016.252), follows the size, velocity and position of droplets reaching a free surface. The resolved K23 adapter derives a quadratic coefficient at the ambient terminal speed and uses buoyancy and relative wind during flight. It reuses the existing falling integrator for each contiguous partition. The flume uses the existing SEA-04 contact source with the actual diameter and normal approach velocity at each interpolated crossing. Compact snow uses Brown and Francis's mass law and Heymsfield and Westbrook's terminal speed. [Proof and limits](whitepaper/reproduce.md#atmo-04-size-resolved-rain-flight-and-field-measurements)

### ICE-04 ordered pack contacts and parallel floe drift

Agnieszka Herman (2016), [Discrete-Element bonded-particle Sea Ice model DESIgn](https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-9-1219-2016), §6.2, separates body forces from contact forces. Mark Hopkins and Alan Thorndike (2004), [Formation of an aggregate scale in Arctic sea ice](https://doi.org/10.1029/2003JC001855), describe the contact and ridging regimes of a granular ice model. Dominic Vella and John Wettlaufer (2008), [Explaining the patterns formed by ice floe interactions](https://doi.org/10.1029/2008JC004781), equation 12, gives the simple rafting thickness for elastic plates. Margo retains its disk model, implicit water drag and fixed contact order. The native participants split only the independent translation and drag, with each substep joining before the contact grid.

Yanzhuo Xue et al. (2024), [A combined experimental and numerical approach to predict ship resistance and power demand in broken ice](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.oceaneng.2023.116476), Table 1 and §2, describe the tow geometry, model floes, concentrations and independently measured material parameters. Table 3 provides repeat-trial resistance at two speeds. The comparison substitutes equal-area disks and a waterline capsule and checks the change in resistance between the two measured concentrations at fixed speed. [Reproduction](whitepaper/reproduce.md#ice-04-native-floe-drift-and-towing-tank-comparison)

### ICE-01 independent column thermodynamics and ordered surface drift

Perry Bartelt and Michael Lehning (2002), [A physical SNOWPACK model for the Swiss avalanche warning, Part I](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0165-232X(02)00074-5), describe the layer-scale heat and mass balances. John Pomeroy and Donald Gray (1990), [Saltation of snow](https://doi.org/10.1029/WR026i007p01583), give the threshold and equilibrium transport used in the current drift phase. Michael Lehning, Henning Löwe, Michael Ryser and Norbert Raderschall (2008), [Inhomogeneous precipitation distribution and snow transport in steep terrain](https://doi.org/10.1029/2007WR006545), separate surface saltation from suspension and preferential deposition. Margo retains the reduced layer balances and the ordered redistribution. Each worker evolves independent columns once the redistributed mass arrives. The accepted state publishes together after checking candidate values.


## Far mountains on the horizon ring and the air's tint in sky-coloured haze (2026-11-28, Above the Treeline round 6)

Problem: past an 8 km world the horizon ring (`@margoengine/biomes` horizon.ts) drew peaks on 128 m texels of ridged
value noise, so a crest was one corner and peaks were straight-sided cones; and the sky fog in the sky's colour gave
every distance the horizon's own white-grey, so far ranges under clear air never turned blue (KB-BIOMES-HORIZONCONE1,
KB-SKY-HAZETINT1).

### ICE-03 independent native iceberg rows and accepted water sources

Justin Burton et al. (2012), [Laboratory investigations of iceberg capsize dynamics, energy dissipation and tsunamigenesis](https://doi.org/10.1029/2011JF002055), §5, give a hydrostatic cuboid comparison and discuss dissipation and added mass. Till Wagner, Alon Stern, Rebecca Dell and Ian Eisenman (2017), [On the representation of capsizing in iceberg models](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ocemod.2017.07.003), §2, give the static aspect-ratio criterion with its density-ratio dependence. This change retains the current clipped-waterline dynamics. Helpers integrate disjoint rows and use the existing f64x2 area and wrench math. The caller checks staged outputs and publishes the ordered calving, wake and freshwater records together.

## Crest teeth and smeared rock faces on the clipmap terrain (2026-11-28, Above the Treeline round 10)

Problem: every clipmap cell was two triangles split along the same diagonal, so a crest running along the other
diagonal was drawn as a row of triangular teeth (the near ridge of the alpine shot; KB-TERRAIN-CRESTTEETH1). With
`TerrainOptions.rock`, the layer colour's triplanar projections were picked by the rock structure's shading normal, so
a bench's near-level normal or a facet's tilt projected the texture along steep faces as streaks
(KB-TERRAIN-ROCKSMEAR1).

Sources read (papers only, no code):
- N. Dyn, D. Levin and S. Rippa, "Data dependent triangulations for piecewise linear interpolation", IMA Journal of
  Numerical Analysis 10(1), 1990, https://doi.org/10.1093/imanum/10.1.137 (choose each quad's diagonal by the data, not
  a fixed rule).
- E. Catmull and R. Rom, "A class of local interpolating splines", Computer Aided Geometric Design, Academic Press,
  1974; R. Keys, "Cubic convolution interpolation for digital image processing", IEEE TASSP 29(6), 1981,
  https://doi.org/10.1109/TASSP.1981.1163711 (the a = -0.5 cubic: a reference height at the cell centre that sees the
  4 x 4 neighbourhood, so it leans toward the crest along a ridge and toward the floor along a valley).
- M. Strugar, "Continuous Distance-Dependent Level of Detail for Rendering Heightmaps", Journal of Graphics, GPU, and
  Game Tools 14(4), 2009, https://doi.org/10.1080/2151237X.2009.10129287 (the vertex morph the centre follows).
- R. Geiss, "Generating Complex Procedural Terrains Using the GPU", GPU Gems 3, ch. 1, 2007 (triplanar projection
  weighted by the surface normal).

Margo's own: a centre vertex per cell, shared only by its own fan, so its choice cannot open a crack; it sits on the
midpoint of the diagonal whose mean height is nearer the cubic height at the centre, following the morphed corners;
the projections read the interpolated surface normal while the structure normal only shades (terrain
test/grid.test.js, test/teeth.browser.mjs, test/rock-projection.test.js).

## A knife-edge ridge sagging between lattice points on the clipmap terrain (2026-11-28, Above the Treeline round 11)

Problem: a clipmap ring's corner snaps to its own spacing, so the finer ring inside it sits up to one finer cell off
its lattice. The ring moved its vertices by that offset times a weight falling linearly from 1 at its inner edge to 0
at its outer edge, which left most of its vertices a fraction of a cell off the heightmap's lattice, where the bilinear
height cuts sharp features: a knife-edge ridge sagged by up to a third of its height (KB-TERRAIN-RINGSAG1).

Sources read (papers only, no code):
- F. Losasso and H. Hoppe, "Geometry clipmaps: terrain rendering using nested regular grids", ACM SIGGRAPH 2004,
  https://doi.org/10.1145/1186562.1015799 (nested rings whose vertices stay on each level's own lattice; the offset to
  the finer level is taken up at the inner edge, by an L-shaped fill strip there).
- M. Strugar, "Continuous Distance-Dependent Level of Detail for Rendering Heightmaps", JGT 14(4), 2009,
  https://doi.org/10.1080/2151237X.2009.10129287 (the morph to the coarser lattice at the outer edge).

Margo's own: the inner edge's vertices move by the whole offset (so they meet the finer ring's morphed outer edge) and
every other vertex stays on its lattice; the first cell row takes up the offset (terrain test/teeth.browser.mjs).

## Snow shelter and wind exposure as ground rules (2026-11-28, Above the Treeline round 11)

Problem: a summer snowfield (`firn`) could be ruled only by height, slope, curvature and temperature, so it lay as
small flecks on the gentle, sunny, wind-scoured tops where real July snow is gone first.

Sources read (papers only, no code):
- B. McCune and D. Keon, "Equations for potential annual direct incident radiation and heat load", Journal of
  Vegetation Science 13(4), 2002, https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1654-1103.2002.tb02087.x (the folded-aspect heat load the
  biomes climate already uses).
- A. Winstral, K. Elder and R. E. Davis, "Spatial snow modeling of wind-redistributed snow using terrain-based
  parameters", Journal of Hydrometeorology 3(5), 2002, https://doi.org/10.1175/1525-7541(2002)003<0524:SSMOWR>2.0.CO;2
  (the Sx upwind exposure the world's `exposure` layer holds; drifts in the lee).
- T. Grunewald, J. Stotter, J. W. Pomeroy and others, "Statistical modelling of the snow depth distribution in open
  alpine terrain", Hydrology and Earth System Sciences 17, 2013, https://doi.org/10.5194/hess-17-3005-2013 (northness,
  Sx and curvature as predictors of snow depth after elevation).
- J. Revuelto, J. I. Lopez-Moreno, C. Azorin-Molina and S. M. Vicente-Serrano, "Topographic control of snowpack
  distribution in a small catchment in the central Spanish Pyrenees", The Cryosphere 8, 2014,
  https://doi.org/10.5194/tc-8-1989-2014 (the same predictors near the melt-out, when patches are what remains).

Margo's own: `GroundLayer.exposure` reads the existing layer; `GroundLayer.shelter` is derived per cell in integers
from slope, aspect, exposure and curvature as the mean of three terms each 0.5 on flat open ground (away from the
sun, lee, hollow), on the tiles and the overview alike (biomes tests/view.test.js).

## Skinning about optimized centres of rotation (2026-11-28, rigging group 9)

`@margoengine/animation/cor` and its default in `@margoengine/humans` `addPerson`. Written from the papers' equations;
no paper's companion code and no other engine's skinning code was read.

- Binh Huy Le and Jessica K. Hodgins, "Real-time skeletal skinning with optimized centers of rotation", ACM TOG
  35(4):37, 2016, https://doi.org/10.1145/2897824.2925959 (the per-vertex centre as the similarity-weighted mean of the
  mesh's triangles, the similarity of two weight sets with sigma 0.1, and the skin: blended rotation about the centre
  plus the linear blend of the centre).
- Ladislav Kavan, Steven Collins, Jiri Zara and Carol O'Sullivan, "Geometric skinning with approximate dual quaternion
  blending", ACM TOG 27(4):105, 2008, https://doi.org/10.1145/1409625.1409627 (the sign-aligned quaternion blend, and the
  bulge on the outside of a bend that the centres remove).
- Ladislav Kavan and Olga Sorkine, "Elasticity-inspired deformers for character articulation", ACM TOG 31(6):196, 2012,
  https://doi.org/10.1145/2366145.2366215 (compared: joint-based deformers that also fix the bulge, set aside because
  they need per-joint fitting, where centres need none).
- Binh Huy Le and J. P. Lewis, "Direct delta mush skinning and variants", ACM TOG 38(4):113, 2019,
  https://doi.org/10.1145/3306346.3322982 (compared: removes both artifacts but needs per-vertex 4x4 precomputed
  matrices per bone, far more memory than one centre; kept for group 10 correctives).
- Rinat Abdrashitov, Kim Raichstat, Jared Monsen and David Hill, "Robust skin weights transfer via weight inpainting",
  SIGGRAPH Asia 2023 Technical Communications (link not yet checked; read for the open garment weight
  fault KB-SKIN-SKIRT1: body-to-garment transfer where the garment is close, inpainting elsewhere; not built yet).

Margo's own: triangles are summed into clusters of like weights (to 1/16 per bone) and indexed by each pair of bones
they hold, so a vertex reads only clusters that share two of its bones (the similarity is zero otherwise); vertices with
the same weights (to 1/4096) share one centre; the centres ride as one more vec4 after each vertex's influences, and
the bones reuse the dual quaternion slots, each rebuilt on the centre for its linear blend. Tests: animation
tests/cor.test.js (a half-weighed panel keeps its area to 1e-3 where linear shrinks it, and reaches less far than dual
quaternions; a 160 degree twist keeps its radius; one bone is exact; split parts agree) and
scripts/animation-cor-tests.js (GPU against the CPU pose on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer).

### EARTH-05 independent plate shapes and pressure cycles

Maximilian Apfelbeck, Sebastian Kuß, Bernhard Rebele and Bernd Schäfer, *A systematic approach
to reliably characterize soils based on Bevameter testing* (2011), report separate circular and
equal-area rectangular experiments. The executable comparison uses the Soil01 circular calibration
from Table 5 at 4.8 mm/s. Its independent references are rectangular Fig. 8 centre values and
whiskers at 22 and 48 kPa. The diagnostic records figure-reading allowance, monotone interpolation
and the 128-to-256 grid difference. [Apfelbeck et al.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jterra.2011.04.001)

Majid Rashidi and Mohammad Gholami, *Non-linear modeling of soil sinkage by multiple loadings
using the finite element method* (2011), report ten serial loads on a rectangular plate. The
diagnostic uses the reported geometry and load schedule. Three sparse Fig. 7 laboratory markers
give the measured normalized response and are excluded from the model input. The study does
not report replicate variance. No figures, lab series or implementation code were copied.
[Rashidi and Gholami](https://www.arpnjournals.com/jabs/research_papers/rp_2011/jabs_0311_255.pdf)

Native resistive-force workers partition complete midpoint pairs from Li, Zhang and Goldman (2013),
Eqs. 1–2 and S8–S9. Each pair produces independent forces and the corresponding moment arms.
The caller joins the pairs and adds their wrench terms in body, strip and sample order to retain
the scalar result. [Li, Zhang and Goldman](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1229163).

### EARTH-08 phased elastic waves and recorded site response

Jean Virieux's second-order staggered P–SV stencil keeps the stress and velocity arrays separate.
The ground solver updates its traction-free boundary, advances disjoint velocity rows and joins
them before advancing the stress rows. Each native lane applies the same arithmetic before and
after the split. The stress phase reads the updated neighboring velocity rows across its halo.
[Virieux (1986)](https://doi.org/10.1190/1.1442147)

The Mashiki profile uses the original NIED KiK-net KMMH16 P–S log as reproduced in Fig. 4.34
of the Japanese National Institute for Land and Infrastructure Management and Public Works Research
Institute, *Study on a Method for Verifying Seismic Performance of Large Box Culverts* (2023).
Later velocity profiles inverted from measured spectral ratios are excluded.
[NIED](https://doi.org/10.17598/NIED.0004) · [NILIM and PWRI, Fig. 4.34](https://www.nilim.go.jp/lab/bcg/siryou/tnn/tnn1247pdf/ks1247.pdf)

The independent density estimate uses Kiyoshi Fukutake et al., *Quantitative strong motion
simulations at three locations in downtown Mashiki during the 2016 Kumamoto Earthquake (Mw 7.0)
based on the nonlinear ground response analyses with soil liquefaction* (2023), Eq. (1).
Dividing the estimated unit weight by reference gravity gives
`1,000 × (1.4 + 0.67 × sqrt(Vs / 1,000))` kg/m³ for Vs in m/s. Weak-motion targets do not
enter this estimate. [Fukutake et al.](https://doi.org/10.1186/s40623-023-01821-8)

Reza Esfahani, Fabrice Cotton and Luis Fabian Bonilla, *Temporal variations of the ‘in-situ’
nonlinear behaviour of shallow sediments during the 2016 Kumamoto Earthquake sequence* (2024),
give independent weak-motion observations in Fig. 2 and §3.1. The diagnostic compares two
synthetic records from a generic incident packet with these observations. Both surface and
downhole motions are simulated. The field reference is excluded from the input and calibration.
[Esfahani et al.](https://doi.org/10.1093/gji/ggae222)

### ICE-05 surface ablation, phase work and measured freezing

J. Ala-Könni, K. M. Kohonen, Matti Leppäranta and Ivan Mammarella compare bulk sensible
heat transfer with four ice-on seasons in *Validation of turbulent heat transfer models against eddy
covariance flux measurements over a seasonally ice-covered lake* (2022). Their bulk sensible term
gives `h = ρAir × cpAir × CH × wind`. The fixed default of 10 W/(m² K) describes only a moderate
neutral wind. Supply the local transfer coefficient or a measured external heat flux for a specific
site. The cold-side Stefan growth and snow resistance remain separate from warm face ablation.
[Ala-Könni et al.](https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-15-4739-2022)

Cecilia M. Bitz and William H. Lipscomb, *An energy-conserving thermodynamic model of sea ice*
(1999), distinguish applied boundary energy and latent ablation. The native work phase uses
independent site pairs for the preset flux's fusion, liquid heating and vaporization. The candidate
remains private until every site's exchange is finite. Internal enthalpy and salt redistribution
remain outside the column model. [Bitz and Lipscomb](https://doi.org/10.1029/1999JC900100)

Bouke Johannes Kaaks, Danny Lathouwers, Jan-Leen Kloosterman and Martin Rohde,
*Transient freezing of water in a square channel: An experimental investigation* (2025), publish
thermocouple fits in Eq. (21) and Table 2 and separate ice thickness measurements in Fig. 7. The
cold plate uses the thermocouple fits. Sixteen sparse optical targets at two stations and two
flow rates are held out. The diagnostic also compares the separately measured bulk water-energy
budget, without using ice growth to infer the heat input. [Kaaks et al.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.expthermflusci.2025.111417)

### FIRE-06 accepted thermal banks, SIMD work phases and measured limits

The existing finite-volume flux and isothermal enthalpy method continue to follow J. Crank,
*Free and Moving Boundary Problems* (1984), H. S. Carslaw and J. C. Jaeger, *Conduction
of Heat in Solids* (1959), and V. R. Voller and C. Prakash, [*A fixed grid numerical
modelling methodology for convection-diffusion mushy region phase-change problems* (1987)](https://doi.org/10.1016/0017-9310(87)90317-6).
Independent f64 pairs decode enthalpy and evaluate the interior stencil. Native participants read the prior
scratch phase, then rendezvous before the next one. Radiation follows the same caller-ordered surface balance
and accepted fields publish after all cells pass. The native shared-memory model uses
[WebAssembly SIMD](https://webassembly.github.io/spec/core/exec/instructions.html#vector-instructions)
and [Wasm threads](https://webassembly.github.io/threads/core/).

C. Gau and R. Viskanta, [*Melting and Solidification of a Pure Metal on a Vertical Wall* (1986)](https://doi.org/10.1115/1.3246884),
supply observed gallium melt fronts. S. Meyer, [*A Fluid Dynamics Approach for Solid-Liquid Phase Change in Binary
and Elemental Melts* (2016)](https://publikationen.bibliothek.kit.edu/1000058183/3880102), clarifies the cavity
orientation and reproduces the observations. Material inputs come from M. W. Chase Jr., [*NIST-JANAF
Thermochemical Tables*, fourth edition (1998)](https://janaf.nist.gov/pdf/JANAF-FourthEd-1998-Gallium.pdf),
[*The Gallium Melting-Point Standard* (NBS, 1977)](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/Legacy/SP/nbsspecialpublication481.pdf),
and M. J. Assael et al., [*Reference correlations for the thermal conductivity of liquid copper, gallium, indium,
iron, lead, nickel and tin* (2017), Eq. 2 and Table 8](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5772911/).
Distances extracted from the observation traces enter only the comparison. The measured spread demonstrates
the limit of the conduction-only model.

The technical ceramic fixture uses high-temperature approximations based on B. Hildmann and H. Schneider,
[*Thermal Conductivity of 2/1-Mullite Single Crystals* (2005)](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1551-2916.2005.00530.x),
the [NIST-JANAF heat capacity of mullite (Chase, 1998)](https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/cbook.cgi?ID=C1302938&Table=on&Type=JANAFS),
and the [BSEE ceramic material properties report, Table 5.2](https://www.bsee.gov/sites/bsee.gov/files/tap-technical-assessment-program/138aa.pdf).
Reported bow is the small-strain equilibrium. The display multiplies displacement by 15 and
renders emission from the simulated surface temperature through the existing spectral glow helper.

### SOUND-04 accepted PCM and independent track work

The native jobs partition whole tracks. Each summed output uses the original ordered mode iteration
and the existing SIMD recurrence updates both real and imaginary coordinates together. Independent PCM
and oscillator work follows the sum of damped modal responses in K. van den Doel, P. G. Kry and D. K. Pai,
[*FoleyAutomatic* (2001), Eq. 1](https://www.cs.ubc.ca/labs/lci/papers/docs2001/van-foleyautomatic.pdf).
Each trial reads the prior accepted oscillators and surface phase, and the caller accepts those banks
and PCM only when every native participant succeeds.

J. F. O'Brien, C. Shen and C. M. Gatchalian,
[*Synthesizing Sounds from Rigid-Body Simulations* (2002)](https://jamesobrien.com/papers/Obrien-SSR-2002-07/index.html)
describes projecting contact forces onto modes computed from geometry. The runtime still accepts supplied
modes. The thin-plate diagnostic uses A. W. Leissa, [*Vibration of Plates* (1969), NASA SP-160](https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19700009156).
For a simply supported rectangular plate, the double sine yields
`omega² = D ((m pi/a)² + (n pi/b)²)² / (rho h)`, where `D = E h³/(12(1-nu²))`.
Material and dimensions are independent of the comparison values in P. Dumond, D. Monette, F. Alladkani,
J. Akl and I. Chikhaoui, [*Simplified setup for the vibration study of plates with simply-supported boundary conditions* (2019)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mex.2019.09.023).
Tables 3–4 furnish nominal geometry and material inputs and Table 5 furnishes both measured frequency series.
The script documents the density unit correction, numerical readout bands and the limits of ideal supports.

The technical striker fixture uses the first elastic free–free Euler–Bernoulli beam mode evaluated from
its displayed bar geometry. The nodal locations illustrate the shape of this mode. Damping and PCM gain are
authored. [F. A. Khasawneh and D. Segalman, *Exact and numerically stable expressions for Euler-Bernoulli
and Timoshenko beam modes* (2019)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.03222).

### BIO-02 staged developmental seasons and parallel light rows

Pałubicki et al., [*Self-organizing tree models for image synthesis* (2009), §4.1](https://algorithmicbotany.org/papers/selforg.sig2009.small.pdf)
describe a voxel penumbra whose contribution weakens with depth below the shade source.
The original integer-layer deposit is retained. Each native participant owns distinct output
rows, visits the same canonically ordered sources and accumulates adjacent x cells with SIMD.
The trial graph and root history update accepted banks together, with the same signed-cell transform.
Prusinkiewicz and Lindenmayer's [*The Algorithmic Beauty of Plants* (1990), chapter 2](https://algorithmicbotany.org/papers/#abop)
provides the concurrent axiom and bud production model. Pirk et al., [*Plastic Trees* (2012)](https://doi.org/10.1145/2185520.2185546)
motivates local obstacles and light avoidance. Re-bending existing wood and shedding remain outside this method.

K. W. Gottschalk, [*Effects of shading on growth and development of northern red oak, black oak,
black cherry, and red maple seedlings. I. Height, diameter, and root/shoot ratio* (1985)](https://research.fs.usda.gov/treesearch/47682),
Tables 2 and 4, supplies the red maple shade-tent observations. The production diagnostic maps
the measured fraction of full light to the solver's sky exposure, uses the generic settings published
before the claim and compares retained height as a separate output. It repeats at a second voxel
size and a prescribed lower water supply. Seasonal species-specific photosynthesis and realized root
water remain outside the diagnostic's input data.

### BIO-03 native shade partitions and retained forest state

Botkin, Janak and Wallis, [*Some Ecological Consequences of a Computer Model of Forest Growth* (1972)](https://www.jstor.org/stable/2258570)
motivate annual cohorts and individual turnover. S. W. Pacala et al.,
[*Forest Models Defined by Field Measurements: Estimation, Error Analysis and Dynamics* (1996)](https://doi.org/10.2307/2963479),
establish the distinction between measured species traits and local competition. P. Köhler and A. Huth,
[*The effects of tree species grouping in tropical rain forest modelling* (1998)](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0304-3800(98)00066-0),
use explicit light-dependent growth and carbon. The engine continues to approximate crown overlap with ordered
integer rows. One participant prepares the spatial table, and a shared native pass queries disjoint candidate rows.
Capping each nonnegative overlap contribution at the total Q16 cover limit preserves saturation and prevents
two broad crowns from overflowing signed accumulation before complete cover is recognized.

R. A. Slesak, M. C. Agne, C. A. Harrington and M. D. Powers,
[*Long-term effects of tree spacing during reforestation on survival and growth of three important
tree species in the Pacific Northwest, USA* (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.foreco.2025.122724),
report measured Douglas-fir survival after 16–40 years. R. O. Curtis, S. Bansal and C. A. Harrington,
[*Relation of Initial Spacing and Relative Stand Density Indices to Stand Characteristics in a Douglas-Fir
Plantation Spacing Trial* (2016)](https://pubs.usgs.gov/publication/70173842), give the stock age and spacing layout.
The simulation uses the published treatments and the pre-claim generic fir ceiling and compares observed
survival separately. The two initial crown radii form an unfitted sensitivity comparison.

F. Brüchert and B. Gardiner, [*The effect of wind exposure on the tree aerial architecture and biomechanics
of Sitka spruce* (2006)](https://doi.org/10.3732/ajb.93.10.1512), measured crown dimensions along windward
and leeward axes. The renderer witness uses the existing growth-area weighting and a civil exposure field,
with authored tree geometry and no calibration of lean to that study.

### BIO-04 accepted patches and native ageing

J. Dorsey and P. Hanrahan, [*Modeling and Rendering of Metallic Patinas* (1996)](https://graphics.stanford.edu/papers/patina/),
separate chemical transformation from diffuse optical transport. J. Gu et al., [*Time-Varying Surface
Appearance* (2006)](https://cave.cs.columbia.edu/old/publications/pdfs/Gu_TOG06.pdf), relate spatial texture
to the timing of appearance changes. The solver keeps independent material patches, applies the existing
Kubelka–Munk readout for their accepted layers, and processes disjoint native blocks without reordering
a column's operations. SIMD handles physical terms shared by consecutive rows and the pinned Rust
transcendentals preserve the existing scalar material branches. The synchronous entry remains available
for callers that create the solver without loading a native kernel.

The atmospheric state continues to use the specified [ISO 9223:2012 dose response](https://www.iso.org/standard/53499.html)
and [ISO 9224:2012 long-term curve](https://www.iso.org/standard/53500.html).
The immersion witness maps a resolved waterline to prescribed uniform-current wet exposure, using the
[ASTM G102-23](https://store.astm.org/standards/g102) Faraday balance for consumed material. The test separates
a real wetting condition from its assumed current and optical parameters.

### BIO-04 independent outdoor corrosion observations

R. Vera et al., [*Corrosion Behavior of Copper Exposed in Marine Tropical Atmosphere in Rapa Nui
(Easter Island) Chile 20 Years after MICAT* (2022)](https://doi.org/10.3390/met12122082), reports
independent copper coupons exposed after the original dose-response calibration. The inputs
come from Table 1 and meteorology in Fig. 3. Penetration read separately from §3.2 and Fig. 6 is
compared after one and three years. L. Paterlini, A. Brenna, F. Ceriani, M. Gamba, M. Ormellese
and F. Bolzoni, [*Atmospheric Corrosion of Different Steel Types in Urban and Marine Exposure* (2024)](https://doi.org/10.3390/ma17246211),
supply a second, bare carbon-steel regime. The ten-month comparison uses independently reported
first-year meteorology as a proxy and the ISO 9223 concentration-to-deposition conversion for SO₂.
The script records extraction precision and climate sensitivity separately from measurement uncertainty.

### SPACE-02 native Table 1 evaluation and eclipse observations

The optional celestial kernel evaluates the same JPL Table 1 elements, Newton iteration count and angular projection order as the existing Margo analytic path. SIMD evaluates pairs of planet rows. The independent partition never reduces across rows, and each participant writes its own work receipt. Pinned trigonometry and the existing Earth–Moon barycentre adjustment preserve the JavaScript result. See [E. M. Standish, Approximate Positions of the Planets, JPL Solar System Dynamics](https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/planets/approx_pos.html) and [P. T. Wallace and N. Capitaine, A&A 459 (2006)](https://syrte.obspm.fr/iau2006/aa06_459.IAU06prec.pdf).

The [measured eclipse diagnostic](../packages/physics/scripts/space02-celestial-measured.mjs) transcribes site coordinates, observed times and camera brackets from observations published after the analytic parameters were established. No timing offset or model parameter is fitted. Earth rotation uses the independent Bulletin B entries for MJD 60054–60055 and 60408–60409. Earth orientation and marked geographic coordinates are model inputs. The flash-spectrum and camera records are the references.

- L. Quaglia, J. Irwin, A. Pessi, L. Kafka and K. Emmanouilidis, [ATSE2023: Using Photodiode Loggers to Estimate the Eclipse Solar Radius, Journal for Occultation Astronomy 2023-4, pp. 16–22](https://iota-es.de/JOA/JOA2023_4.pdf). Cape Range Site 1 was independently surveyed and timed.
- L. Quaglia, J. Irwin and A. Pessi, [Experimentally Assessing the Accuracy of Eclipse Path Maps, Journal for Occultation Astronomy 2024-4, pp. 3–12](https://iota-es.de/JOA/JOA2024_4.pdf), with [observer site map](https://www.besselianelements.com/eclipse-maps-accuracy/). The Stephenville and Gunter comparisons use the observers' GPS and camera findings.
- USNO/IERS, [finals2000A.all Bulletin B Earth orientation data](https://maia.usno.navy.mil/ser7/finals2000A.all). These orientation observations are independent of the eclipse contact reports.

### SPACE-03 private native disk trials and observational geometry

The native disk keeps the Pringle finite-volume tridiagonal operation and the face-flow and luminosity sums in radial order. The publication phases evaluate disjoint pairs of annuli without inter-worker reductions. The six accepted fields remain private until every candidate row, face and ledger is finite. The staged update preserves the archived implementation's floating-point operation order. See [James E. Pringle, Accretion Discs in Astrophysics, 1981](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev.aa.19.090181.001033) and [Donald Lynden-Bell and James E. Pringle, The Evolution of Viscous Discs and the Origin of the Nebular Variables, 1974](https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/168.3.603).

- Edward Teo, [Spherical Photon Orbits around a Kerr Black Hole](https://doi.org/10.1023/A:1026286607562), 2003, equations 1 and 10. The equatorial critical orbit is the double root of the radial null potential. Production exterior trajectories independently bracket critical impact parameters from capture and return. Changing launch radius and phase step quantifies the numerical bracketing error.
- GRAVITY Collaboration, [A geometric distance measurement to the Galactic center black hole with 0.3% uncertainty](https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/201935656), 2019, Table 1 noise model. Pre-EHT stellar dynamics fixes the mass and distance used to convert vacuum widths to sky angles.
- Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration, [First Sagittarius A* Event Horizon Telescope Results. I. The Shadow of the Supermassive Black Hole in the Center of the Milky Way](https://doi.org/10.3847/2041-8213/ac6674), 2022, and [IV. Variability, Morphology, and Black Hole Mass](https://doi.org/10.3847/2041-8213/ac6736), 2022. The independent 230 GHz image measures an emission-ring diameter. Its finite thickness and the model-dependent mapping to a vacuum critical curve bound the interpretation of the comparison. No EHT observation sets a solver parameter.

### SOFT-03 native point prediction and independent bending observations

The existing framed rod and inextensible guides use disjoint point prediction under the common world gravity and sampled air-relative drag. A pair of SIMD rows preserves each point's arithmetic and scalar quaternion update. The rod and reciprocal contact corrections retain the original order and operate on the private trial. See [Tassilo Kugelstadt and Elmar Schömer, Position and Orientation Based Cosserat Rods, 2016](https://diglib.eg.org/items/eb5dd4ac-529c-4d6b-86ab-454cec714272), [Matthias Müller, Tae-Yong Kim and Nuttapong Chentanez, Fast Simulation of Inextensible Hair and Fur, 2012](https://diglib.eg.org/items/11db9962-07b8-46a1-ab46-ecc9ee05086d), and [Florence Bertails et al., Super-Helices for Predicting the Dynamics of Natural Hair, 2006](https://doi.org/10.1145/1179352.1142012).

The measurement script transcribes four independent force/deflection markers from [M. A. S. Akanda, H. Tohmyoh and M. Saka, An Integrated Compact Unit for Wide Range Micro-Newton Force Measurement, 2010](https://doi.org/10.1299/jmmp.4.545), section 4.1 and figure 7(a). The diameters, spans and applied loads define the trial. The published deflections are withheld from the solver. The existing 3 GPa default is used without fitting, including without the modulus fitted by the paper to the same plot. A tip-local wind callback supplies the measured quasistatic load, and re-running with lower numerical settling mass separates static bending from assumed settling dynamics. The test does not infer properties of hair clumps or horse bundles.

### LIFE-01 acceptance of ground contacts and measured gait bounds

The biped and quadruped wrapper uses the same independent contact and body phases as the optional GroundLocomotion kernel. The planted spring model follows [Reinhard Blickhan, The spring-mass model for running and hopping, 1989](https://doi.org/10.1016/0021-9290(89)90224-8). Relative leg length and speed follow the dynamic similarity approach of [R. McNeill Alexander and A. S. Jayes, A dynamic similarity hypothesis for the gaits of quadrupedal mammals, 1983](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1469-7998.1983.tb04266.x). The trial exposes prepared contact samples to the rigid reaction accumulator before accepting both sets of outputs. Fixed-order body partitions and their work counts remain unchanged.

[A. I. Gmel et al., walking and trotting treadmill measurements, 2024](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jevs.2024.105005), Tables 1, 2 and 4, provide independently observed belt speeds, cohort masses, cadence, stance fractions and fore/hind impulses. Only belt speed and mass enter the representative bodies. The cadence and load partition are separate scoring columns. The diagnostic compares the original leg geometry and independent geometry and speed variation. It documents cohort deviations and model differences without fitting either.

The fixed-camera stance test uses diagonal trotting footfalls as described in [Milton Hildebrand, Symmetrical Gaits of Horses, 1965](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.150.3697.701), together with the actual sampled terrain plane and a common Coulomb friction budget.

### LIFE-05 signed walking trials and station measurements

The new native schedule retains the existing spatial sort, neighbour order and accumulation. Independent walker drives and per-walker wall tests and travel are separate native phases. The original strict order applies to each wall list and every walker-to-walker impulse. Relative velocities and the XZ dot products retain their f64x2 order. See [Ioannis Karamouzas, Brian Skinner and Stephen J. Guy, Universal power law governing pedestrian interactions, 2014](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.113.238701), equations 2–3, for time-to-collision anticipation and [Jur van den Berg et al., Reciprocal n-body collision avoidance, 2011](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-19457-3_1) for the separate NavMesh avoidance path.

[Armin Seyfried, Bernhard Steffen, Wolfram Klingsch and Maik Boltes, The fundamental diagram of pedestrian movement revisited, 2005](https://doi.org/10.1088/1742-5468/2005/10/P10002), Figure 2 and Table 1, supply the observed 17.3 m loop and 2 m station, published widths and straight lengths, walkers and extracted station speeds. The simulation keeps the existing free speed. It transcribes sparse reported mean speeds as comparison facts and leaves the paper's fitted spacing-speed curve outside the model. Interpolated line crossings and a shape and wall-resolution study bound the simulation's numerical sampling.
